structure.title: ANOTHER YEAR OF RECORD-BREAKING NUMBERS
key_items: BUSINESS AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE - EICHER MOTORS LIMITED
structure.summary: Eicher Motors Limited reports record-breaking financial performance for 2024-25. Key metrics include: 10,02,893 motorcycles sold, up 10% YoY; revenue from operations at ₹18,870 Crores, up 14% YoY; EBITDA at ₹4,712 Crores, up 9% YoY; operating margin (EBIT) at ₹3,983 Crores, up 7% YoY; share of profit from JV (VE Commercial Vehicles) at ₹700 Crores, up 56% YoY; and total comprehensive income at ₹4,504 Crores, up 13% YoY. VE Commercial Vehicles sold 90,161 commercial vehicles, up 5% YoY, with revenue from operations at ₹23,548 Crores, up 8% YoY, and EBITDA (excluding other income) at ₹2,023 Crores, up 18% YoY. Note that VECV revenue and EBITDA are not consolidated in EML's consolidated figures; VECV's share of profits is accounted as a single line in the P&L.

structure.title: DRIVEN BY LEGACY, POWERED BY VISION
structure.summary: Eicher Motors Limited (EML), a Chennai-based global automobile company listed on BSE and NSE, owns Royal Enfield and co-owns VE Commercial Vehicles (VECV). EML's market cap as of March 31, 2025, is ₹1,46,615 Crores, with 33% YoY growth. Royal Enfield, the oldest motorcycle brand in continuous production since 1901, offers premium models like Bear 650, Classic 650, Guerrilla 450, Hunter 350, Meteor 350, Super Meteor 650, Interceptor 650, Continental GT 650, Shotgun 650, Himalayan 450, Scram 440, Bullet 350, Classic 350, and Goan Classic 350, designed in UK and India. Royal Enfield unveiled Flying Flea, an electric urban mobility brand, with FF.C6 and FF.S6 expected by early 2026. VECV, a joint venture with AB Volvo, delivers commercial vehicles, engines, and distribution for Eicher, Volvo Trucks, and Volvo Buses.

structure.title: PURE MOTORCYCLING WITH ROYAL ENFIELD
structure.summary: Royal Enfield's 'Pure Motorcycling' philosophy emphasizes authentic, real riding experiences at one's own pace, preserving the feeling of riding an Enfield. It highlights the brand's 124-year history and its role as a guardian of authenticity for riders seeking self-discovery. The text defines 'Pure' as a fundamental, sensorial connection with oneself and surroundings, free from external approval and artificiality, and 'Motorcycling' as the active pursuit of riding, owning, maintaining, caring, and workmanship, focusing on essentials and reconnecting with the purity of the experience. It also references the 2024-25 Integrated Annual Report corporate overview.

structure.title: PURPOSE-LED GROWTH IN MOTORCYCLING AND COMMERCIAL MOBILITY
key_items: VE COMMERCIAL VEHICLES (VECV) MOBILITY THAT MOVES NATIONS
structure.summary: Eicher Motors Limited (EML) operates with a purpose-led growth strategy focused on engineering excellence and future-ready mobility through two verticals: Royal Enfield and VE Commercial Vehicles (VECV). Royal Enfield, a global mid-size motorcycle brand (250cc–750cc) present in 65+ countries, reported FY 2024-25 domestic sales of 9,02,757 units and an 87% market share in India's mid-size segment. Its portfolio includes motorcycles across Classics, Cruisers, Scramblers, Roadsters, Adventure Tourers, and Neo-Retro Sport, plus riding gear, apparel, and accessories, with UK/India tech centres, Indian manufacturing, 2,000+ retail outlets, and the Flying Flea initiative. VECV, a joint venture with Volvo Group, sold 90,161 commercial vehicles in FY 2024-25, entered the small truck segment with Eicher Pro X, and holds a 36% market share in light & medium duty CVs and 21.4% in buses. Its portfolio spans Eicher trucks and buses, Volvo premium vehicles, connected mobility, engines and components, and electromobility leadership.

structure.title: VECV PERFORMANCE
structure.summary: VECV's FY2024-25 performance highlights market leadership in LMD trucks, 90,161 vehicles sold (5.4% growth), SCV expansion with an electric-first approach, record HD and bus sales, over 90 product variants, new Pro 8035XM tipper, network expansion to 1,082 touchpoints, Volvo FM 420 Road Train launch, new electric and LNG offerings, digital upgrades, and industrial investments in automation and AI. Employee engagement scored 85, with recognitions including CII HR Excellence and five Apollo CV Awards. Business segments cover Eicher Trucks and Buses, Volvo Trucks and Buses India, international operations, Eicher Engineering Components, VE Powertrain, and new subsidiaries for IoT and Indonesian supply chain. Subsidiaries, associate, and JV details include VECV South Africa, VECV Lanka, PT VECV Automotive Indonesia, VE Electro-Mobility, and VE Connected Solutions, which delivered over 32,000 telematics devices and began ADAS Level 1 and 2 development.

nodes.title: VECV PERFORMANCE (intro)
nodes.summary: VECV's FY2024-25 performance highlights market share leadership in LMD trucks and gains across segments, driven by customer centricity, technology, and operational excellence. Milestones include 90,161 vehicles sold (5.4% growth), SCV portfolio expansion with electric-first approach on an all-woman assembly line, LMD industry leadership, record HD and Bus sales, over 90 product variants, launch of the Pro 8035XM 8X4 Tipper with automatic transmission, network expansion to 1,082 touchpoints (123 company-owned), Volvo FM 420 Road Train launch, new electric and LNG offerings, digital capability upgrades, industrial infrastructure investments with automation and AI, employee engagement score of 85, and recognitions like the CII HR Excellence Award and five Apollo CV Awards. The organization remains committed to 'Transform to Perform' for future readiness.

nodes.title: OUR BUSINESSES, MARKET AND FUTURE PROSPECTS
nodes.summary: The text covers Eicher Motors' business segments: Eicher Trucks and Buses achieved record sales, production, and operational excellence, entered the SCV segment, and reported bus plant output and EV workshop progress. Volvo Trucks India led premium segments, achieved service revenue milestone, advanced LNG technology, and launched a road train. Volvo Buses India saw record coach sales and customer additions. International business grew exports, introduced Euro V vehicles, telematics, and incorporated an Indonesian subsidiary. Eicher Engineering Components achieved record revenue and expanded capabilities. VE Powertrain delivered record engines. New subsidiaries VECS and PT VECV Automotive Indonesia were established for IoT/telematics and vehicle supply chain, respectively.

nodes.title: SUBSIDIARIES, ASSOCIATE AND JOINT VENTURE COMPANIES
nodes.summary: The text covers VECV's subsidiaries, associate, and joint venture companies during FY 2024-25. It details the formation of VE Connected Solutions (VECS) as a JV with iTriangle Infotech. It reports on VECV South Africa's flat market, 200 unit sales, three new dealers, and growing aftersales. VECV Lanka notes Sri Lanka's economic recovery, industry growth from 400 to 1,150 units, and resumption of vehicle imports. PT VECV Automotive Indonesia was incorporated for strategic expansion, with operations on track. VE Electro-Mobility expanded electric bus deployment under 'Bus as a Service'. VECS developed and supplied over 32,000 telematics devices, initiated segment-specific connected solutions, and began ADAS Level 1 and 2 development.

nodes.title: VE CONNECTED SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED – A SUBSIDIARY COMPANY

VECS designed and began supplying advanced telematics devices for factory fitment across VECV's product portfolio, delivering over 32,000 devices in its inaugural year across BUS, LMD, and Pro X ranges. It also initiated delivery of segment-specific connected solutions for high-growth applications and began in-house development of ADAS Level 1 and Level 2 solutions, supporting VECV's digitalization roadmap and marking entry into advanced driver assistance technologies.

structure.title: ROOTED IN HERITAGE. DRIVEN BY INNOVATION.
structure.summary: Siddhartha Lal transitions to Executive Chairman of Eicher Motors Limited (EML), outlining his focus on strengthening governance through board reconstitution, new appointments, and an ESG council. He highlights the strong performance of Royal Enfield and VE Commercial Vehicles, emphasizing growth potential, operational agility, and strategic investments in electrification while maintaining internal combustion technology. Lal discusses the need to navigate a technology shift, prioritize long-term value, and foster a culture of innovation. The text also covers record financial results for FY 2024-25, including consolidated revenue, EBITDA, and PAT, and expresses gratitude to predecessor Mr. Sandilya.

structure.title: RIDING AHEAD WITH PURPOSE AND PASSION
structure.summary: Royal Enfield's FY 2024-25 was its strongest financial year, achieving record revenue, profit, and EBITDA, surpassing one million annual sales (10.02 lakh units, up 10%), with domestic growth of 8% and international growth of 30%. The festive season saw over 100,000 units sold in a month. Six new motorcycles were launched, including the Bear 650, Guerrilla 450, Scram 440, Classic 350, Classic 650, and Goan Classic 350. Milestones included the Hunter 350 crossing 500,000 units and the Super Meteor 650 surpassing 50,000 units. The brand won 12 global design and innovation awards and was ranked #1 in J.D. Power initial quality. The Flying Flea electric mobility brand was introduced at EICMA. The spares business grew 13%, new warehouses opened, and the dealer network expanded. Internationally, new manufacturing and assembly operations were established in Brazil, Thailand, and Bangladesh, with over 100,000 units sold outside India. Eicher Motors' VECV recorded best-ever annual sales, and a dividend of ₹70 per share was recommended. Royal Enfield's Social Mission consolidated with the completion of the Himalayan Hub and the launch of Green Pit Stops.

structure.title: WE’RE NOW #1 IN THE MIDSIZE SEGMENT IN THE UK, #2 IN ARGENTINA, #3 IN BRAZIL, AND #5 IN THE EU.
structure.summary: The text highlights Royal Enfield's UK midsize segment #1 ranking and other market positions, ongoing UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage documentation in the Himalayas (90+ practices), return of Ice Hockey League and Spiti Cup, and the inaugural Journeying Across the Himalayas festival with 50 communities, 100 partners, 150 experts, 200 artists, and 6,000+ visitors. Social Mission reached 1.5 lakh people directly (83% vulnerable) and 37 lakh indirectly, with CSR across 14 states, one UT, and 15 aspirational districts. It marks the 125th year, emphasizing legacy and start-up agility, guided by REBALANCE strategy focusing on product focus, capabilities, global markets, lifestyle portfolio, and apparel. It addresses plural mobility (ICE and EV coexistence), sustainability, and celebrates one million motorcycles, ending with a shareholder message from B. Govindarajan.

structure.title: ACCELERATING GROWTH. POWERED BY TRUST.
structure.summary: This shareholder letter highlights Eicher Motors' record FY 2024-25 performance, with both Royal Enfield and VE Commercial Vehicles (VECV) achieving best-ever results. It details VECV's 17-year Volvo Group JV progress, including the electric-first Eicher Pro X range on an all-woman assembly line, Volvo Trucks India's first FM Road Train, LNG-powered truck deliveries, and expanded EV portfolio. Financially, VECV delivered 90,161 vehicles (5.4% growth vs. industry's 0.3%), revenue of ₹23,548 crores, EBITDA at 8.8%, and PAT up 56.8%, leading the 5-18.5T truck segment. Eicher Engineering Components won global OEM orders, and Eicher Power Solutions expanded. The letter notes India's resilient economy, infrastructure spending, ESG, and digital adoption as growth drivers, and thanks stakeholders.

nodes.summary: Royal Enfield launched the Nirvik V2 all-weather riding jacket and the Guerrilla 450 roadster on the Sherpa platform. It unveiled the 2024 Classic 350 with new colorways, livery, modern upgrades, personalization, and declared the 'Year and Decade of the Classic'. The company pioneered an industry-first Borderless Warranty Programme covering 3,000+ service points in 70+ countries. It opened its first exclusive apparel store in Pune and introduced the Crossroader, India's first titanium-powered CE-certified dual-sport riding jacket.

nodes.summary: The page covers Royal Enfield's launch of the Guerrilla 450, a modern roadster on the Sherpa 450 platform, emphasizing street performance and fun. It also details the 2024 Classic 350 edition with new colorways, livery, modern upgrades, and personalization via the Factory Custom Programme, alongside the 'Year and the Decade of the Classic' initiative. Additionally, it highlights the industry-first Borderless Warranty Programme, a global initiative allowing riders warranty access across borders, backed by over 3,000 service touchpoints in 2,605 cities across 70+ countries, enhancing customer care and satisfaction.

nodes.title: OPENED ROYAL ENFIELD’S FIRST EXCLUSIVE APPAREL STORE IN PUNE
nodes.summary: Royal Enfield opened its first exclusive apparel store in Pune's Amanora Mall, offering gear, lifestyle apparel, and accessories. It launched the Crossroader, India's first titanium-powered, CE-certified dual-sport riding jacket. The third edition of The Great Himalayan Exploration, in partnership with UNESCO, documented intangible cultural heritage with National Geographic India filming. Royal Enfield also collaborated with C.L.A.W. Global to launch Unlimit, an adventure and mindset training initiative in the Himalayas focused on resilience, sustainability, and community empowerment.

nodes.title: ART OF MOTORCYCLING SEASON 4 TRANSPORTS PARTICIPANTS TO THE YEAR 3000 AD
nodes.summary:
ART OF MOTORCYCLING SEASON 4 TRANSPORTS PARTICIPANTS TO THE YEAR 3000 AD
The global Y3K edition of #ArtOfMotorcycling expanded its reach globally to new APAC & LATAM regions, inviting participants to reimagine the relationship between mankind, technology, and the pursuit of freedom on two wheels in the year 3000 AD. With entries open across four categories and a league of global judges, submissions were also evaluated by social polls giving the global creative community a voice in the decision-making process.

nodes.title: LAUNCHED AN EXCLUSIVE WOMEN’S WEAR COLLECTION AND FIRST SUSTAINABLE RIDING JACKET FOR WOMEN
nodes.summary: Royal Enfield launched an exclusive women’s wear collection and its first sustainable riding jacket for women made from recycled materials. It announced early-bird registrations for Motoverse’s fourteenth edition, featuring new elements like 'Ride to Motoverse' and a Spotify partnership. The brand celebrated the 20th Himalayan Odyssey with 122 riders covering 3,050 km and debuted the Great Himalayan Adventure Festival. It marked nine decades of the Bullet 350 with the 'Battalion Black' edition and two years of the Hunter 350 with a 'Hunter Day' ride involving 8,000 riders. Additionally, it introduced a state-inspired Regional T-Shirt Collection with 16 designs.

structure.title: GOAN CLASSIC 350
structure.summary: The text introduces the Goan Classic 350, a Royal Enfield motorcycle as a tribute to 1970s Goan moto-culture. It describes the design inspired by bobber-style customs with heritage aesthetics, relaxed posture, floating single seat, mid-ape handlebars, chopped fenders, and whitewall tyres on edge-laced tubeless spoke wheels. It highlights the 349cc air-oil cooled engine for smooth cruising, signature bobber styling, four vibrant colourways, and its appeal to riders preferring the slow lane on their own terms.

structure.title: ECHOES OF GOA. ESSENCE OF A CLASSIC.
structure.summary: This text covers Royal Enfield's Goan Classic 350, a bobber-style motorcycle inspired by Goa's 1970s-80s counterculture and custom scene, with design features like chopped fenders, mid-ape handlebars, whitewall tires, and colorways. It details the 349cc engine (20.2 bhp, 27 Nm), 5-speed gearbox, chassis, dual-channel ABS, and modern features including LED lighting, USB-C charging, and Tripper navigation, plus custom accessories. The text notes its launch at Motoverse 2024, a Rafu'D fashion collaboration capsule collection, the ACKO Drive Viewer's Choice Award, and media reviews. It then briefly introduces the Classic 650 Twin as a refined evolution with a parallel twin engine.

structure.title: BUILT TO BE RIDDEN. DESIGNED TO BE ADMIRED.
structure.summary: The text introduces the Royal Enfield Classic 650 as a new chapter in the Classic series, featuring a 648cc parallel twin engine for smooth cruising. It details design cues like the frame-loop, teardrop tank, and LED headlamp, alongside comfort features such as a wide seat, upright bars, and a digital LCD dash. Chrome and aluminium touches echo post-war British styling, and it is available in Teal, Vallam Red, Bruntingthorpe Blue, and Black Chrome liveries. The text connects the model to the 1948 500 Twin and its swinging arm suspension innovation, and notes its global debut at EICMA 2024 in Milan with EMEA pricing announced, highlighting its forward-leaning stance and timeless silhouette.

structure.title: GLOBAL MEDIA RECEPTION
structure.summary: The text compiles global media reviews of the Royal Enfield Classic 650 Twin. Critics praise its strong brand recall, design, ability to handle triple-digit speeds, natural ride, refinement, and value. It is described as a larger, more powerful, premium iteration of the Classic 350, with an imposing, timeless design and exceptional quality. The bike offers an upright riding stance, a punchy and smooth engine, and sportier performance than its appearance suggests. Reviewers note it suits those upgrading from the Classic 500 and seeking a classic-styled motorcycle with modernisation, comfort, and highway capability without fuss.

structure.title: BEAR 650
structure.summary: The text introduces the Royal Enfield Bear 650, a new scrambler motorcycle inspired by Eddie Mulder's 1960 Big Bear Run win. It highlights the bike's blend of 60s scrambler styling with modern performance on the 650 Twin platform, designed for both city and trails. Key features include dual-purpose tyres, a kicked-up rear loop, a scrambler seat, a toughened stance, and five colorways including a tribute shade 'Two Four Nine'. The text also includes a quote from Fast Eddie and references to the annual report.

structure.title: BUILT ON GUT, DRIVEN BY GUT FEEL
key_items: MADE FOR THE GUTSY. INSPIRED BY HISTORY.
structure.summary: The text introduces the Royal Enfield Bear 650, a scrambler built on the 650-Twin platform, highlighting its 47 bhp, 56.5 Nm torque, 2-1 exhaust, dual-purpose tyres, contoured seat, and five colourways. It details the reinforced chassis, Showa USD forks, twin-tube RSUs, 184mm ground clearance, 19"/17" wheels, and ergonomics. Features include the Tripper Dash TFT console with Google Maps, USB-C charging, Wingman Connectivity, LED lighting, and black aluminium switch cubes. It references the 1960 Big Bear Run and Eddie Mulder's victory as inspiration, and notes the global launch at EICMA 2024. Positive media reviews from Bikewale, Motoring World, Overdrive, Auto X, Acko Drive, Cycle World, and Motorcycle.com are summarized, along with the CarandBike Scrambler Motorcycle of the Year award.

structure.title: FLYING FLEA
structure.summary: This section introduces Flying Flea, Royal Enfield's new City+ electric motorcycle brand inspired by the 1940s original. It covers the product line-up (FF.C6 and FF.S6), design innovations like the forged aluminium Girder fork, frame, and magnesium battery case, and connected technology featuring an in-house OS with Qualcomm and NXP processors, TFT display, voice assist, and OTA updates. It also details design philosophy and collaborations with Rkive City, Mattia Biagi, Ansh Kumar, Goji, and Lekha Rathnam, positioning Flying Flea as a cultural catalyst. Additionally, it highlights Royal Enfield's 2024-25 updates: the Bullet 350 Battalion Black edition with all-black aesthetics, gold pinstripes, and refined performance; the Himalayan 450 with tubeless spoke wheels; and the new Scram 440 with a 443cc engine, 6-speed gearbox, tubeless wheel options, top box mounting, and two variants (Trail and Force) in five colors, unveiled at Motoverse 2024, emphasizing the blend of heritage and innovation.

structure.title: RIDE-READY INNOVATION. RETAIL-READY EXPERIENCE.

MotoVille offered workshops on customization and storytelling, along with Royal Enfield lifestyle apparel and accessories. The festival fostered belonging among diverse attendees. structure.title: Art of Motorcycling (Season 4)
structure.summary: Art of Motorcycling (Season 4)

structure.title: REIMAGINING MOTORCYCLING IN THE YEAR 3000 AD
structure.summary: Royal Enfield's Art of Motorcycling Season 4, themed 'Y3K,' invited global creators to envision future motorcycling culture across 12 countries. The Y3K edition featured four categories: Gen AI, Digital Art, Handcrafted Design, and Comic Art, supported by virtual masterclasses, graffiti installations, collaborations, and a jury panel including Aaquib Wani and others. The season included masterclasses, city graffiti activations, and collaborative collections with Daily Objects and FARAK, transforming winning designs into streetwear and accessories. Finalists were chosen via jury curation and community voting; seven winners received an all-expenses-paid trip to Motoverse 2024, where their works were exhibited as exclusive merchandise. Select creators appeared on Motoverse Vox Pops, and the Comic Art winner earned a collaboration opportunity. The 2024 edition evolved the contest into a global movement.

structure.title: MOTORSPORTS AND CUSTOMS
key_items: FROM STREET TO CIRCUIT: A HOMEGROWN LEGACY ON THE TRACK
structure.summary: The text covers the Royal Enfield Continental GT Cup 2024, a one-make championship partnered with JK Tyre Motorsport, featuring 3 rounds and 8 races on Indian circuits with 24 finalists (12 professional, 12 amateur) riding the GT-R650. It highlights the cup's role in nurturing talent and building a motorsport community. Additionally, it details the Royal Enfield Track School, which trained over 250 riders across five cities, and the Slide School, which trained over 1,200 riders globally, including the inaugural Slide School Cup in Europe and India. The text also includes impact metrics: 5K+ participants and 24 finalists.

structure.title: Royal Enfield Continental GT Cup 2024 and Track School
key_items: A SEASON OF PROGRESS AND POSSIBILITY
TRACK SCHOOL: BUILDING SKILL, CONFIDENCE AND COMMUNITY
structure.summary: The 2024 Continental GT Cup season began at the Madras International Circuit with a competitive grid of experienced and emerging riders on refined GT-R650s, balancing grit with camaraderie. Beyond racing, the Cup supports Royal Enfield's vision of building a motorcycling ecosystem through the Track School, which lowers entry barriers and offers structured pathways to professional racing. The 2024 edition highlighted the Cup as a platform for growth and learning. The Track School provides foundational racing skills and a pathway to the Cup, making track training accessible across India; it has empowered over 250 riders in five cities, with four dedicated schools in Coimbatore training 80 more riders in six months, fostering a safer, more capable riding community on and off the track.

structure.title: SLIDE SCHOOL: SPREADING THE ART OF FLAT TRACK RIDING
structure.summary:
SLIDE SCHOOL: SPREADING THE ART OF FLAT TRACK RIDING
Royal Enfield’s Slide School offered riders a dedicated space to master the unique art of sliding in a controlled and safe environment. With over 1,200 riders trained across multiple locations worldwide, Slide Schools remained both accessible for newcomers and rewarding for experienced riders. This year also
saw the launch of the inaugural Slide School Cup in Europe and India. In Europe, riders from three countries competed, culminating in a finale at the prestigious DTRA. India’s edition kicked off at Motoverse, with three regional rounds in Bangalore, Pune, and Jaipur, leading up to the grand finale at Royal Enfield’s Jaipur Track in Kukas, where regional champions and media riders battled it out.

Other collaborations include a fully-faired Continental GT with Top Gear, the Wildfire retro rally racers with Death Spray Customs, and the 3X BOB Builds on the HNTR platform. structure.title: TOGETHER, WE RIDE DEEPER
structure.summary: Royal Enfield emphasizes its rider community, united by passion for motorcycling. It nurtures bonds through purpose-driven rides and gatherings celebrating exploration and culture. Curated rides include high-altitude expeditions, long-haul explorations, lifestyle trails, and culture-led weekend getaways, offering bucket-list journeys difficult to do solo. These experiences foster camaraderie and connection, making the ride as meaningful as the destination. The text also references community-led celebrations within the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.

structure.title: RIDING TOGETHER, RISING AS ONE
structure.summary: The section covers Royal Enfield's global riding events and community celebrations, including the Himalayan Adventure Tibet through Tibet and Nepal, World Motorcycle Day with citywide rides across India, the 20th Himalayan Odyssey to Umling La and Siachen, and the Hunter Day Ride celebrating the Hunter 350's anniversary. It details expeditions like the Himalayan Adventure Changthang across Ladakh, the Uncover Northeast Ride blending music and motorcycling to the Ziro Festival, the Himalayan Adventure Manang in Nepal, and One Ride 2024 uniting riders in 66 countries. Regional events include the North Bengal Ride through Eastern Himalayan hill towns, the Meteor 350 Araku Valley Ride, the Desert Diary Rajasthan Tour covering Alsisar Mahal, Jodhpur, Udaipur, and Pushkar, and the Tour of the Northeast 2025 exploring Cherrapunjee, Shillong, Kaziranga, Tawang, and more.

nodes.title: Royal Enfield Riding Events and Community Celebrations
key_items: 20 TH EDITION OF THE HIMALAYAN ODYSSEY
nodes.summary: The page highlights Royal Enfield’s passion-driven motorcycling community and four key events. The Himalayan Adventure Tibet (May 12–26, 2024) took riders through Tibet and Nepal on the new Himalayan, blending spirituality, nature, and culture. World Motorcycle Day 2024 (June 22–23) featured citywide rides across six Indian metros with races and maze chases. The 20th Himalayan Odyssey was an 18-day, 3,050 km ride to Umling La and Siachen Base Camp with 122 global riders, ending at the Great Himalayan Adventure Festival in Leh. The Hunter Day Ride in August 2024 celebrated the Hunter 350’s second anniversary with over 8,000 riders in 700+ cities, including factory tours and community events.

nodes.title: HIMALAYAN ADVENTURE CHANGTHANG
nodes.summary: The text covers four Royal Enfield riding events/expeaditions: the Himalayan Adventure Changthang ride across Ladakh's high-altitude desert with unpaved trails and lakes; the Uncover Northeast Ride from Guwahati to the Ziro Festival in Arunachal Pradesh on Meteor 350, blending music and motorcycling; the Himalayan Adventure Manang 2024 in Nepal, an 8-day journey on the Himalayan 450 from Besishahar to Manang at 3,500m through gorges and remote villages; and One Ride 2024, the 13th global ride uniting riders across 66 countries under the theme 'Be Bold. Be Seen. Be One.' with over 16,000 participants in 490 Indian cities.

nodes.title: Corporate Overview: Northeast Ride and Himalayan Adventure
nodes.summary: The page presents a corporate overview describing two motorcycle expeditions. The Uncover Northeast Ride, starting September 2024, combined music, motorcycling, and community on a Meteor 350 from Guwahati to the Ziro Festival in Arunachal Pradesh, celebrating culture amid the Eastern Himalayas. The Himalayan Adventure Manang 2024 was an 8-day journey on a Royal Enfield Himalayan 450 through Nepal's high-altitude wilderness from Besishahar to Manang at 3,500 meters, featuring steep gorges, remote villages, and views of Dhaulagiri, Manaslu, and Annapurna, offering cultural immersion in a remote region.

nodes.title: ONE RIDE 2024 UNITES RIDERS ACROSS 66 COUNTRIES

Be One,' with significant participation in India, Asia-Pacific, Europe, Latin America, and North America. It also describes the North Bengal Ride 2024 through Eastern Himalayan hill towns, the Meteor 350 Araku Valley Ride from Bhubaneswar to Vizag, and the 10-day Desert Diary Rajasthan Tour 2025 covering Alsisar Mahal, Jodhpur, Udaipur, and Pushkar.

nodes.title: RIDERS EXPLORE RAJASTHAN’S HERITAGE TRAILS ON DESERT DIARY 2025
nodes.summary:
RIDERS EXPLORE RAJASTHAN’S HERITAGE TRAILS ON DESERT DIARY 2025
Royal Enfield’s Desert Diary Rajasthan Tour 2025 unfolded over 10 days across the sun-soaked landscapes of India’s desert state. The route kicked off in Gurugram and covered Alsisar Mahal, Jodhpur, Udaipur, and Pushkar – fusingCORPORATE OVERVIEW
open highways with heritage properties and off-road desert trails. With 18 Super Meteor 650s and full logistical support, the journey celebrated the spirit of exploration through sweeping roads, local culture, and immersive riding experiences.

nodes.title: TOUR OF THE NORTHEAST 2025
nodes.summary:
TOUR OF THE NORTHEAST 2025
Spanning 13 days from January 17 to 30, the Tour of the Northeast 2025 offered riders an expansive exploration of one of India’s most diverse and scenic regions. Starting in Guwahati, the ride traversed Cherrapunjee, Shillong, Dawki, Jowai, Kaziranga, Majuli, Ziro, Bhalukpong, Dirang, and Tawang. From the wildlife of Kaziranga and the spiritual calm of Tawang Monastery to the cascading beauty of the Garden of Caves, the journey immersed riders in Northeast India’s natural grandeur and layered cultural identity.

structure.title: MANUFACTURING EXCELLENCE AND EXPERTISE
key_items: Highlights of the current manufacturing setup include: Vehicle assembly
structure.summary: EML's manufacturing excellence is built on globally benchmarked practices, lean systems, and a skilled workforce, with DNV-certified plants and SRK methodology achieving a 50% reduction in fault frequency. Quality frameworks deployed across CKD operations ensure consistency while preserving Royal Enfield's 'Made Like a Gun' quality. The setup includes flexible vehicle assembly with 1,990+ SKUs, 90+ Poka Yoke systems, and full vehicle testing; engine assembly with 100% DC nutrunner tightening, 520 Poka Yoke interventions, and semi-automated testing; surface finishing with 46 robots, corrosion protection, gloss measurement, and 54 colors; machining with 367 centers, 32 robotic washing, 19 robotic deburring machines, and online SPCs; fabrication with 100% robotic welding using 98 robots, laser welding, and robotic washing; and auto buffing with a two-stage automated planetary process, robotic cells, and an engineered dust extraction system.

key_items: Key initiatives during the year include:

Operational cost optimisation was pursued through workforce rationalisation, automation, and reduced overheads. Capex spending rose from 521 Crores in FY21 to 629 in FY22, 654 in FY23, 808 in FY24, and 1,010 in FY25.

structure.summary:
WHERE THE ROAD MEETS RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE PEOPLE AROUND
EML, through the Royal Enfield Social Mission, continued to deepen its social impact in FY 2024-25 with strategic community partnerships, capacity-building programmes and grassroots conservation efforts across the Himalayan region and other geographies of operation. With climate resilience and community empowerment at its core, the initiatives touched lives, strengthened traditional knowledge systems, enabled nature- linked livelihoods, and nurtured the fragile Himalayan ecosystem. structure.title: BUILDING RESILIENCE IN THE HIMALAYAS -THE HIMALAYAN HUB
key_items: Himalayan Hub FY 2024-25 Highlights; Overall, across three years; Circularity initiative highlights FY 2024-25
structure.summary: The text outlines EML's Himalayan Hub initiative under the Royal Enfield Social Mission, aiming to build resilience in 100 Indian Himalayan communities by 2030 and mobilize one million riders for sustainable living. FY 2024-25 highlights include operationalizing hubs in Theog (Western) and Tezpur (Eastern), engaging nearly 200 young changemakers through fellowships and grants. Western outreach details a residential fellowship for 24 fellows, capacity building for 109 community members, and a creative practitioners cohort. Eastern outreach covers 22 fellows from 19 communities, a responsible tourism conclave, and 88 conservation grant proposals. It also mentions circularity initiatives processing over 880 MT waste, reducing 25 MT CO2, and earning over ₹10 lakhs from recycled material. Additional programs include wellness, youth for forest, river conservation, and storytelling.

structure.title: GREEN PIT STOPS (GPS)
key_items: FY 2024-25 Highlights; Kharu, Ladakh: A Living Cultural Stop
Kharu, Ladakh: A Living Cultural Stop
Babeli, Himachal Pradesh: Sustainable by Design
structure.summary: The Green Pit Stops (GPS) initiative by Eicher Motors provides eco-conscious services and livelihood opportunities for local SHGs, especially women, along riding routes. FY 2024-25 highlights include two operational/under-construction sites (Kharu, Ladakh and Babeli, Himachal Pradesh), a third site at Manas National Park with DPR completed, and training for SHGs in hospitality, accounting, baking, handicrafts, and traditional cuisine. Kharu, launched in June 2024, served 4,500+ travelers and generated ₹9+ lakhs, with SHG women catering major events. Babeli uses Dhajji-Diwari construction and trained 70+ women in food processing and knitting. The initiative was featured in a multimedia exhibit. The text also introduces The Himalayan Knot, a flagship textile conservation project protecting traditional craftsmanship and pastoral communities.

It also details The Great Himalayan Exploration (TGHE) Edition III, which documented 26 Intangible Cultural Heritage practices via 56 rider-researchers in Ladakh and Sikkim, partnered with UNESCO and National Geographic, and promoted behaviour change through water security, road safety, education, and healthcare efforts.

The Western edition covered 16 practices with 42 riders and expert insights, partnering with National Geographic for a series. The Eastern edition documented 10 practices with 14 riders. TGHE also drives behavior change through water security, road safety, and community support, and was featured at the Journeying Across the Himalayas festival with exhibitions. Collaborations include LAMO for cultural mapping and MUSE for water security. Testimonials highlight participant experiences.

structure.title: SPORTS, EDUCATION & HEALTH
structure.summary: The Royal Enfield Social Mission operates in Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand, focusing on sports, education, and health in high-altitude regions. The initiative addresses water resilience through community mobilization and ecological restoration, including planting 8,000 saplings. Winter sports programs include the Royal Enfield Ice Hockey League Season 2 (330 players, 15 teams, 7,000 spectators), Spiti Cup Season 2, training 32 grassroots coaches, Learn to Play reaching 950+ young players, and the Changthang Football Initiative engaging 380 students. Education efforts include Project-Based Learning for 410 students in Kargil, winter learning camps across 17 centers with 35 youth facilitators, a Zero-Waste School challenge in 39 Uttarakhand schools with 2,890 students, and Bhoti language classes for 210 community members. Health initiatives with CEVA, MUSE, and local hospitals screened 3,200+ patients and performed 57 surgeries, focusing on preventive care and awareness. The text also includes a player testimonial and a coach's endorsement of the Ice Hockey League.

structure.title: BIODIVERSITY & CONSERVATION
structure.summary: The text covers Royal Enfield's biodiversity initiatives under UN SDGs, focusing on high-altitude, forest, riverine, and marine ecosystems. It details keystone species protection for snow leopards (surveys, community conserved area), golden langurs (awareness campaigns, recovery plan), Himalayan brown bears (solar lighting, youth training), and forgotten cats (documentation, naturalist training). Nature-linked livelihoods include birdwatching training, nature festivals, moth species discovery, and youth naturalist training. Marine conservation covers olive ridley turtle nests, marine animal rescues, ghost net recovery, and collaborations. Cultural-ecological stewardship involves yak herder associations, yak wool processing, and women's training. Awareness through art features exhibitions and VR experiences. A partnership quote from Nature Conservation Foundation is included, along with report attribution.

structure.title: ROAD SAFETY
structure.summary: Royal Enfield's Helmets for India (HFI) programme promotes road safety through behavioural change, community outreach, and creative expression. FY 2024-25 highlights include a Helmet Art Roadshow across 4 cities with 250+ participants in workshops and #ArtOfSafety rides reaching 550+ road users; the Ziro Festival featuring a sustainable helmet installation viewed by 15,600+ visitors with 80+ customisation participants; engagement at Motoverse 2024, Homegrown Festival, and other events; road safety exhibits with India Foundation for the Arts showcasing custom helmets and inclusive artwork by Aravani Art Project and 11 other artists; and training 92 community members in Basic Life Support along the Manali-Darcha corridor in Himachal Pradesh with Lady Willingdon Hospital. The text also includes an artist's statement by Indu Antony on using the helmet as a symbol of childhood experiences and self-liberation, and references UN SDGs.

structure.title: BEHAVIOUR CHANGE COMMUNICATION
structure.summary: The text describes EML's Behaviour Change Communication programme, integrating public art, behavioural science, and cultural engagement to promote sustainable, safe, and inclusive practices in Himalayan communities and riding circuits. In FY 2024-25, it reached new audiences through immersive festivals, community research, and cross-disciplinary collaborations. A research-led pilot with Behaviour Smart studied rider and community perspectives across 8 Himalayan locations, identifying behavioural barriers to responsible riding, plastic reduction, and cultural immersion, with insights to inform interventions from FY 2025-26. Art for awareness included two art-based interventions at the Sā Ladakh Festival using sustainable fibres and performance to highlight pashmina and wool journeys, and Thangka-inspired signage in Spiti promoting refill culture and Buddhist art. Culture as catalyst included commissioning 'Abundance in Scarcity' at Serendipity Arts Festival and the first edition of 'Journeying Across the Himalayas' hosting 200+ artists, 50+ communities, and 6,000+ visitors over five days. Key outcomes: 87% increased awareness, ₹35+ Lakhs in sales, and 4.2 Million media reach. The festival hosted the first EGF Partners' Meet (105 attendees) and is supported by a catalogue and impact report with Art X. Quotes from Urvashi Butalia and Puneeta Chadha highlight the festival's inclusive and experimental nature and the Himalayan Bazaar's showcase of community products.

structure.title: LOCAL AREA DEVELOPMENT
structure.summary: EML's local area development initiatives align with UN SDGs, focusing on holistic community upliftment through WaSH, health, skilling, climate resilience, waste management, and safety. Health and sanitation efforts include menstrual hygiene awareness, 50 toilets, RO plant, solar street lights benefiting 2,000+ families in Sriperumbudur, and water system rejuvenation in Eraiyur with rainwater harvesting, soak pits, ponds, drainage, and sponge gardens, plus 50 household rainwater harvesting units. Skilling at Royal Enfield Technical Academy trained 1,267 candidates with 100% placement. Waste management in Masinagudi covered 13,000 households, processing 2+ MT waste/day, won a Clean Village Award, and built a ₹6 Lakhs corpus. Public safety includes lifeguard towers at Kovalam saving 88 lives, and two school buses in Mysuru improving attendance.

structure.title: GROUP PROJECTS
structure.summary: This text outlines EML's group projects supporting UN SDGs through education and healthcare partnerships. The Shikshak Pahal programme with Bodh Shiksha Samiti supports 32 community schools in Alwar, reaching 4,975 students, with outcomes including a 99.75% pass rate, 195 teachers trained, 1,453 community members engaged, infrastructure upgrades in 14 schools, a new school inauguration, and nutrition and health check-ups. EML's support to Dr. Shroff's Charity Eye Hospital includes OPD renovation, construction of new facilities, patent filings for Retinoblastoma research, and an Indo-Japan DST grant for research exchange.

structure.title: EDUCATION SYSTEM STRENGTHENED
structure.summary: The text highlights FY 2024-25 achievements in strengthening education systems through strategic project management with The Education Alliance in Tamil Nadu and Punjab. In Punjab's Hunar Sikhiya programme, 37,500 schools, 18 lakh students, and 2.5 lakh teachers were impacted, with AI curriculum rollout in high schools, mobilization of ₹100 crores (₹69 crores deployed), and 93% teacher completion of spoken English training. In Tamil Nadu, over 6.5 lakh students were assessed via baseline evaluations, a Project Management Unit was set up for 40 schools, 100 classrooms/labs were constructed impacting 2,000+ students, 750 students received JEE/NEET coaching with 130 clearing Mains, and the admission process was digitized statewide. The text aligns with UN SDGs and is from an integrated annual report.

structure.title: DISASTER RELIEF & RESPONSE
structure.summary: The text covers Royal Enfield's disaster relief and response efforts aligned with UN SDGs, detailing FY 2024-25 interventions: housing and education support for 11 Gaddi families in Himachal Pradesh after monsoon damages, and immediate relief including bedding kits and essentials for 3,000 families across 13 villages in Tamil Nadu post-Cyclone Fengal. It also addresses EML's sustainability strategy, focusing on minimizing environmental impact through resource efficiency, clean energy adoption, carbon footprint reduction, water positivity, circularity, and stakeholder collaboration to advance a planet-positive future via employee, community, and supply chain engagement.

structure.title: TRANSITIONING TOWARDS A LOW-CARBON FUTURE
structure.summary: The text outlines Eicher Motors Limited's transition to a low-carbon future, targeting an 80% reduction in emission intensity (tCO2e/motorcycle) by FY 2029-30 from a FY 2020-21 baseline. In FY 2024-25, it achieved a 0.62 GJ/motorcycle energy intensity, a 51% reduction in emission intensity from FY 2023-24, an 84% renewable electricity mix, and a 56% reduction in carbon emissions from the FY 2020-21 baseline, impacting SDGs. It details ISO 50001:2018 certified energy management systems across major plants, key initiatives such as process-level optimization (compressor waste heat recovery, heat pumps, VFDs, lower-capacity cooling towers), upgrading to efficient equipment (VFDs, LED lighting, Articmaster), and reducing electricity usage (solar street lights, skylight tubes). It provides the energy consumption mix for FY 2024-25 (diesel, LPG, LNG, petrol, electricity, renewable solar) and energy savings achieved from FY 2019-20 to FY 2024-25.

structure.summary: Eicher Motors Limited (EML) has implemented ISO 50001:2018 certified energy management systems across major manufacturing plants to optimize energy consumption, reduce costs, and lower environmental impact. structure.title: SUSTAINING WATER-POSITIVE OPERATIONS
structure.summary: This text covers EML's water-positive operations, including targets and impact: maintaining water positivity across all plants and global headquarters for the sixth consecutive year, with total water recycled/treated at 3,90,282 KL, reused at 4,41,075 KL, and water intensity of 0.23 KL/motorcycle. structure.title: REDUCING AND MANAGING WASTE
structure.summary:
REDUCING AND MANAGING WASTE
EML has significantly reduced solid wastes generated across various stages of operations by deploying various measures. Paper usage has been eliminated, helping save trees and environmental impact. The Company stringently follows the practice of treating all hazardous wastes before disposal.
Further, various initiatives have been taken to effectively manage wastes including converting sewage sludge into vermicompost and generating biogas from waste food for use in cooking. Wastes like ETP/ phosphate/paint sludge, powder, residue containing oil, and filter waste are co-processed in cement kilns. Plastic wastes are managed as per statutory Extended Producer Responsibility norms under PWM Rules, 2016.

structure.title: RECYCLING AND REUSING WASTE
structure.summary: The text covers EML's recycling and reuse initiatives, including zero liquid discharge plants for wastewater treatment and reuse, and studies to enhance motorcycle part recyclability with 97% reusability achieved in FY 2024-25. It then details EML's governance framework: a one-tier Board with 63% Independent Directors, separation of Chairman and Managing Director roles effective February 13, 2025, and a culture of responsible conduct through a Code of Conduct and zero tolerance for unethical behavior. Key governance policies are listed, including Code of Conduct, Whistleblower Policy, Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Policy, Insider Trading Code, Board Diversity Policy, Materiality Policy, CSR Policy, and Policy on Material Subsidiaries. Finally, it describes the ESG Council's role in strengthening ESG oversight, reporting to the Risk Management Committee.

structure.title: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS
key_items: Indian Two-Wheeler Industry; Global Motorcycle Industry
About VE Commercial Vehicles Ltd (VECV):; Board changes at EML; FY 2024-25: Another great year for Royal Enfield
FY 2024-25: Another great year for Royal Enfield
structure.summary: The text covers the Management Discussion and Analysis, starting with an economic overview of India's GDP growth at 6.5% in FY 2024-25, inflation trends, RBI's repo rate cut, IIP growth, GST collections, PMI, per capita income, and CPI inflation. It then discusses the subdued global economy with 3.3% growth, persistent inflation, high interest rates, and geopolitical tensions, noting moderating but above-target inflation in key markets. The industry overview details the Indian two-wheeler industry's 9.1% growth, segment-wise performance, electric two-wheeler growth, and the global motorcycle industry reaching 61.8 million units with India leading growth and exports up 21.4%. The company overview introduces Eicher Motors Limited, its subsidiary Royal Enfield, and VE Commercial Vehicles, including board changes. Finally, it highlights Royal Enfield's FY 2024-25 performance with record sales, market share gains, and international expansion.

structure.title: REBALANCE - A STRATEGIC LONG-TERM VISION
structure.summary: The text introduces REBALANCE, Royal Enfield's strategic framework for long-term business resilience, rooted in Pure Motorcycling and harmony between rider, machine, and terrain. It details four pillars: Products (ICE & EV) focusing on best-in-class motorcycles and EV innovation; Brand Led CX redefining customer journeys beyond transactions; Growth Focus balancing scale with profitability and agility with discipline; and Sustainability aligning social and commercial objectives for balanced environmental and community impact. It also covers the July 2024 launch of the Guerrilla 450, a modern roadster on the Sherpa 450 platform with a 452cc liquid-cooled DOHC engine delivering 40 PS and 40 Nm, a steel twin-spar chassis, and strong traction among younger riders in India and Europe.

structure.title: CLASSIC 350 - THE EVERGREEN LEGACY
structure.summary: The text covers Royal Enfield's 2024-25 motorcycle launches: the refreshed Classic 350 with LED, USB-C, Tripper Navigation, seven colors, five variants, and a Factory Custom Programme; the Goan Classic 350 bobber-inspired derivative with floating seat, chopped fenders, whitewall tires, four colors, and Goan heritage; the Bear 650 scrambler with revised chassis, 2-1 exhaust, dual-purpose tires, 184mm clearance, and modern electronics; the Scram 440 ADV crossover with 443cc engine, 6-speed gearbox, switchable ABS, and 795mm seat height; and the Classic 650 revealed at EICMA 2024, featuring the 650 Twin engine and classic styling.

structure.title: PRODUCT INNOVATIONS & GEAR
key_items: Bullet 350 - Battalion Black; Tubeless wheels for Himalayan 450; Crossroader - Dual sport titanium jacket; Women’s wear collection
Royal Enfield x SENA – Advanced Rider Communication
Royal Enfield x Qualcomm – Next-Gen Connected Platform
structure.summary: Royal Enfield launched the Bullet 350 Battalion Black with timeless design, introduced tubeless wheels for the Himalayan 450, and unveiled the Crossroader titanium jacket for dual-sport riders. It also launched its first Women’s Wear Collection with sustainable jackets and gear. The brand partnered with SENA for the 50S Mesh Communicator and with Qualcomm for Flying Flea’s connected platform. Motoverse 2024 in Goa drew 10,000 enthusiasts and featured the Goan Classic 350, Scram 440, and FT450, plus new formats like Revv’ed Up Runway and Motobrew. A Spotify collaboration highlighted music and motorcycling. At EICMA 2024, Royal Enfield launched Flying Flea, its new EV brand, with the C6 and future S6 models.

structure.title: Royal Enfield Motoverse 2024 and Spotify Collaboration Highlights
key_items: SPOTIFY X ROYAL ENFIELD: FUSION OF MUSIC AND MOTORCYCLING
structure.summary: The page covers Royal Enfield's Motoverse 2024 in Goa, which drew nearly 10,000 enthusiasts and featured the launch of the Goan Classic 350, the debut of the Scram 440, and the first public appearance of the FT450 flat track motorcycle, kicking off the Slide School Cup. It also details the deepened collaboration with Spotify for World Music Day and World Motorcycling Day 2024, highlighting indie and hip-hop talent through events like RADAR and RAP 91, and activation at Motoverse with live performances and interactive zones using Spotify's audio tools. Additionally, the page mentions new Motoverse formats such as the Revv'ed Up Runway fashion show, Motobrew collaboration, and community spaces like MotoReel and Art of Motorcycling, emphasizing increased international participation and the event's role in brand-building and rider engagement.

structure.title: EICMA 2024: FAST-FORWARD. REWIND.
structure.summary: At EICMA 2024 in Milan, Royal Enfield showcased heritage and innovation by launching Flying Flea, its first electric vehicle brand, with the Classic-styled C6 model and plans for a Scrambler-styled S6. The brand also expanded its 650cc portfolio in Europe with the Classic 650 and Bear 650, blending old-school elegance and scrambler spirit. Design collaborations like the Shotgun 650 x ICON and Guerrilla 450 x El Solitario 'Prometeo' custom builds highlighted Royal Enfield's growing global influence in motorcycling and custom culture.

structure.title: MARQUEE RIDES AND EVENTS
structure.summary: The text details Royal Enfield's 2024 marquee rides and events: the Continental GT Cup Season 4 with the Twin Power Trophy and winners; the Himalayan Adventure Tibet ride through Nepal and Tibet; World Motorcycle Day city rides across six metros with influencers and activities; the 20th Himalayan Odyssey to Umling La and Siachen with 122 riders and a festival; the Hunter Day ride across 700+ cities with 8,000+ participants; the Himalayan Adventure Changthang high-altitude expedition; and Uncover North East combining motorcycling with the Ziro Festival. These initiatives highlight grassroots racing, adventure riding, community engagement, and cultural experiences.

structure.title: GROWTH FOCUS
key_items: Royal Enfield - India Performance; i. Retail Network; Financing
structure.summary: The text covers Royal Enfield's India performance in FY 2024-25, highlighting sustained growth, dominant market share in the middleweight (87.1%) and >125cc (30.1%) segments, record quarterly sales, and successful product launches including the Goan Classic 350, Guerrilla 450, and Bear 650, with the Hunter 350 surpassing 500,000 cumulative units. It also details retail network expansion with large-format dealerships, studio stores, and the REOWN pre-owned vertical in over 230 cities, retention of #2 rank in FADA Dealer Satisfaction Survey 2024, financing initiatives that raised finance penetration to 61% via low down-payments, extended tenures, and the RE App's digital marketplace, and customer experience innovations like the Assured Buyback Programme with flexible tenures and guaranteed buyback value. Historical sales and market share data from FY19 to FY25 are included.

structure.title: INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS
key_items: International Volume Split (%); Americas; Europe, Middle-East, and Africa (EMEA)
structure.summary: Royal Enfield's FY 2024-25 international performance covers volume recovery and growth despite macroeconomic pressures, with a volume chart from FY19 to FY25 and a regional split: SAARC 17%, APAC 13%, EMEA 44%, Americas 26%. The Americas remained the largest market outside India, with growth in Brazil and Latin America, 324 retail stores, an estimated 8% North American middleweight share, and CKD facility expansion in Brazil. EMEA maintained UK leadership in mid-size motorcycles, grew in Italy, France, Spain, and Germany, added 42 locations, launched the Extra Mile Retail Development Programme, partnered with AW Rostamani in the UAE, and debuted in Turkey with Kibar Holding, holding about 9% EMEA middleweight share and ranking among Europe's top four brands. APAC grew in Thailand, Indonesia, and Bangladesh, opened a fully-owned CKD plant in Thailand, reached 200+ outlets, formed collaborations (Project Origin, Taichi Apparel, TAT), ranked #2 in Thailand and Korea and #3 in Australia, held about 9% APAC share, and in Nepal scaled CKD with four models, 10,000+ units sold, and 38% share in the >125cc segment. The Bullet 350 won Gold at the 7th Japan Bike of the Year Awards 2024.

structure.title: SAARC*
structure.summary:
SAARC*
In a significant move to bolster our international footprint, The Company announced the commencement of operations of its Manufacturing Unit (Category 2) and flagship showroom in Bangladesh. Set up in collaboration with IFAD Motors, this announcement is a significant boost to the company’s business in the SAARC region, and further reiterates Royal Enfield’s commitment to Bangladesh. Located in Chauddagram, Cumilla District, the new manufacturing facility is Royal Enfield’s seventh assembly unit outside India - after Nepal, Brazil (2 facilities), Thailand, Colombia, and Argentina - in addition to its state-of-the-art manufacturing and ancillary facilities located in Tamil Nadu, India.

structure.title: NON-MOTORCYCLE BUSINESS
key_items: After sales, Service and Spare parts; Genuine Motorcycle Accessories
After sales, Service and Spare parts
structure.summary: The text covers Royal Enfield's non-motorcycle business growth in FY 2024-25, with revenues of ₹2,750 Crores (12.8% of overall revenues), spanning apparel, accessories, and aftersales. After-sales ranked #1 per FADA Survey 2024, with new RE Essentials products, improved RSA tracking, and a service cost calculator. Spares achieved ~99% availability with 24-hour delivery. Genuine Motorcycle Accessories expanded with 60 new SKUs and greater configurator adoption. Apparel launched exclusive stores, new campaigns, a digital magazine cover, lifestyle accessories, and won awards. Manufacturing excellence included new CKD units in Bangladesh and Thailand, crossing 1 million units production, a new control tower, and a sustainability award for the Vallam plant.

structure.title: SUSTAINABILITY
structure.summary: This text outlines Royal Enfield's FY 2024-25 sustainability initiatives under its REBALANCE framework. It covers green business operations—energy management with 60% renewable energy mix and 1 MW solar plant, emission reduction of 53.3% per motorcycle and 46% Scope 1&2 reduction, water management with zero liquid discharge and water-positive indices, waste management achieving zero waste to landfill and compressed biogas use, and sustainable packaging with FSC-certified cartons. It also details brand-led social missions: partnering 100 Himalayan communities by 2030, The Great Himalayan Exploration with UNESCO, the Game Changer ice hockey blueprint for Ladakh, and Helmets for India road safety. Finally, it highlights corporate sustainability rankings, including top 30-percentile in global auto, top 10 in MSCI, and #8 in Sustainalytics.

structure.title: HUMAN RESOURCES
structure.summary: The text covers the company's Human Resources focus over the past year on capacity building and employee engagement. Capacity building included over 100,000 training hours for the entire workforce to enhance functional, managerial, and leadership capabilities. Specific measures: Transformational Leadership Program (31 team managers) and Emerging Leadership Program (45 managers); functional programs for skill-building, agility, and future-readiness; People Manager Development Programs; EV-readiness training modules; and the launch of Gurukulam learning initiative in June 2024 for continuous growth and lifelong learning. Employee engagement efforts focused on maintaining an empowered, synergetic, harmonious, and transparent work environment that values meritocracy and innovation to drive passion for the brand.

structure.title: ENTERPRISE RISK MANAGEMENT
key_items: Mitigation Strategy:; Mitigation Strategy:; Mitigation Strategy:
structure.summary: The text outlines the Company's enterprise risk management framework, detailing the Risk Management Committee's role and eight key risks with mitigation strategies: brand relevance tied to ICE platforms and shifting preferences; regulatory compliance across global standards; changing consumer behavior and EV transition; supply chain vulnerabilities; cybersecurity and data privacy threats; geographic concentration and geopolitical risks; human capital and succession planning; and profitability volatility from raw material costs. Each risk includes specific mitigation actions, relevant capitals, and material issues, covering strategic, operational, financial, and human capital dimensions.

structure.title: INTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEMS AND THEIR ADEQUACY
structure.summary: The text outlines the Company's strong internal control framework, covering monitoring, asset safeguarding, fraud prevention, accounting precision, risk management, productivity, and legal compliance. It details the FY 2024-25 assessment affirming effective internal controls over financial reporting, strengthened via the IC-CoE project creating a risk and control matrix. The IC-CoE provides centralized specialist support and collaborates with project owners. It highlights the SAP-based ERP system's system-based checks, governance risk and compliance frameworks, independent Internal Audit monitoring per Audit Committee schedule, statutory auditor review of financial controls, and a whistle-blower policy enabling stakeholders to report wrongdoing without fear.

structure.title: FINANCIAL REVIEW
key_items: Total Sales; Net Revenue from Operations; EBITDA and EBITDA Margin
Net Profit After Tax and EPS
structure.summary: Eicher Motors' FY 2024-25 financial review highlights record annual volumes of 1,002,893 units and revenue of ₹18,870 crores, up 14% YoY. Domestic and international sales, non-motorcycle revenue (₹2,750 crores, 14.6% of consolidated), EBITDA (₹4,712 crores, 25% margin), PAT (₹4,734 crores, up 18.3%), and EPS (₹172.76) are detailed. Cash position (₹16,376 crores), operating cash flow (₹3,980 crores), and capital investment (₹1,024 crores) are noted. Key financial ratios for consolidated and standalone entities are listed, including inventory turnover, current ratio, trade payables turnover, net capital turnover, operating and net profit margins, return on equity, return on capital employed, and basic/diluted EPS.

structure.title: VE COMMERCIAL VEHICLES
structure.summary: The text covers VE Commercial Vehicles' record year, detailing India's FY 2024-25 economic backdrop (GDP growth, infrastructure spending, geopolitical risks), CV industry stability with 0.6% growth and segment trends (HD truck decline, bus growth), policy focus on modernization and local production, and VECV's 5.4% sales growth to 90,161 units, highlighting SCV entry with electric-first Pro X, LMD leadership, and record HD truck and bus sales with innovative products.

structure.title: BUSINESSES, MARKET AND FUTURE PROSPECTS
structure.summary: Eicher Trucks and Buses achieved record FY 2024-25 sales of 87,724 units (up 5.6%), leading the LMD segment and exceeding 20,000 bus sales. Industrial production reached 88,471 vehicles with quality improvements via automation, IoT, AI, and the Volvo Production System. The bus plant produced 8,157 built-up buses, contributing to 10,280 total deliveries. Volvo Trucks India led the premium segment with 1,819 units, grew non-coal volumes to 32%, advanced LNG tractors in e-commerce, and surpassed ₹1,000 crore in after-sales revenue. Volvo Buses India posted record coach sales of 618 units (up 81.2%). Exports grew 39.2% to 5,181 units, driven by innovations, entry into Indonesia, and expansion in the Middle East, Africa, and South Asia. Eicher Engineering Components achieved record revenue over ₹2,000 crore (up 23%), established an axle assembly line for Eicher Pro X, operationalized Plant III for exports, and enhanced automation and sustainability. VE Powertrain delivered a record 60,155 engines, surpassing 400,000 cumulative engines. VE Electromobility deployed over 60 electric buses, fulfilled orders for 40+ electric buses (including 15 for Kochi Metro), and secured an order for 496 buses under the PM-e-Bus Sewa Scheme. VECV expanded its service and sales network by 149 touchpoints to 1,082, enhancing customer experience.

structure.title: VECV
structure.summary: VECV's section covers FY 2024-25 industry data, market share, and customer-centric initiatives including network expansion to 1,082 touchpoints, MyEicher App growth, Uptime predictive diagnostics, and site support. It details innovation through the Eicher Pro X launch, over 90 new products, 36 technologies, Euro 5 Middle East range, and EV/hydrogen advancements, plus sustainability efforts like 4.5 MW solar, water recycling, and tree planting. Subsidiary performance in South Africa, Sri Lanka, and Indonesia is outlined. The outlook highlights India's CV industry growth, VECV's Transform to Perform agenda, over 500 electric trucks/buses and 20 million electric km, expansion into SCVs and international markets, and BRSR disclosures on corporate identity and business activities.

nodes.title: Enhanced Customer Experience through Superior Service, Superior Uptime and Retail Excellence
nodes.summary: The text presents Eicher Motors Limited's industry data for VECV, covering market share and growth for FY 2024-25 versus FY 2023-24 across domestic segments (Cargo, LMD, HD, SCV, Buses), exports, VECV total, and Volvo Trucks and Buses. It also details customer-centric initiatives: expansion of service and sales network by 149 touchpoints to 1,082, growth of the MyEicher App covering over 350,000 vehicles, Uptime initiative benefiting over 180,000 vehicles with predictive diagnostics, and expanded Site Support spanning 355 sites for over 17,500 vehicles, all aimed at enhancing customer experience, uptime, and operational reliability.

nodes.title: Focus on Innovation, Technology upgrade and new products
nodes.summary: VECV launched the Eicher Pro X small truck, introduced over 90 new products and variants, and showcased 36 new technologies on Innovation Day. Developments included Euro 5 range in the Middle East, Truck AC regulatory readiness, and customer seeding of Pro X Diesel/CNG variants, plus advancements in EV and hydrogen (H2-ICE) technologies. Sustainability initiatives: 4.5 MW rooftop solar, 52,000 KL water recycling, and 66,000 trees planted. Subsidiaries: VECV South Africa sold 200 units and expanded dealers; VECV Lanka resumed imports; PT VECV Indonesia was incorporated. The outlook is positive with growth expected in key CV segments, despite geopolitical risks. VECV’s “Transform to Perform” agenda, over 500 electric trucks/buses sold, 20 million electric km clocked, and expansion into SCVs, international business, buses, and components support long-term growth.

nodes.title: Towards Sustainable future; Subsidiaries:
nodes.summary:
EICHER MOTORS LIMITED
Towards Sustainable future
In FY 2024-25, VECV made significant strides towards sustainability, reinforcing its roadmap for achieving Net Zero and carbon neutrality. Key initiatives included enhancing renewable energy capacity with a 4.5 MW rooftop solar installation aimed at reducing emissions by 25%, recycling 52,000 KL of water through an artificial lake at the Bhopal plant and planting 66,000 trees to offset 660 tonnes of CO2 emissions.
Subsidiaries:
VECV South Africa operated in a flat market, recording sales of 200 units, while expanding its dealer network by three new outlets and strengthening aftersales infrastructure.
VECV Lanka benefited from improved market conditions, resuming imports from February 2025 and positioning itself for recovery and growth.
PT VECV Automotive Indonesia was incorporated during the fiscal year and progressed towards operational readiness as part of VECV’s strategic regional expansion.

nodes.title: LOOKING AHEAD
nodes.summary: The text covers India's strong economic momentum and positive FY 2025-26 outlook for the Commercial Vehicle industry, driven by consumption, infrastructure, and policy, with growth in Heavy-Duty Haulage, Intercity Buses, and Small Commercial Vehicles, despite geopolitical and tariff risks. It highlights VECV's 'Transform to Perform' agenda, robust product pipeline, digitalization, and global expansion. VECV's green mobility efforts include over 500 electric trucks/buses, 20 million electric kilometers, and clean fuel technologies (LNG, CNG, hydrogen). Expansion into SCVs and international business enhances growth. The Company is confident in its strategy for long-term stakeholder value. Additionally, the BRSR Section A discloses Eicher Motors Limited's corporate identity, listing details, reporting boundary, assurance provider, and business activities, with 100% turnover from automobiles and 85.4% from motorcycle manufacturing.

nodes.title: Independent Assurance Statement for Eicher Motors BRSR Core
key_items: to the Management of Eicher Motors Limited
nodes.summary: This page is an independent assurance statement from DNV Business Assurance India to the management of Eicher Motors Limited regarding the company's Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) disclosures, including BRSR Core, for FY 2024-25. It presents DNV's conclusion that the BRSR Core Key Performance Indicators under nine ESG attributes are reported in accordance with the Industry Standard on Reporting of BRSR Core. The scope covers a reasonable level of assurance for Eicher's operations across India under direct operational control. Reporting criteria include SEBI circulars and the Greenhouse Gas Protocol. The assurance methodology follows DNV's VeriSustainTM protocol V6.0, ISAE 3000 (revised), and ISO 14064-3 for greenhouse gas disclosures.

nodes.title: Basis of our conclusion
nodes.summary: The text outlines the basis of DNV's assurance conclusion for Eicher's BRSR Core disclosures, detailing a multi-disciplinary team's activities: reviewing KPIs under 9 ESG attributes, evaluating systems and controls, assessing operational boundaries, gathering evidence through stakeholder engagement, conducting on-site and remote audits based on site contribution and complexity, interviewing senior managers, and verifying consolidated performance against the VeriSustainTM Protocol for reasonable assurance. It lists inherent limitations, including a ±5% materiality threshold, exclusion of financial data (relying on third-party audits for specific attributes), restriction to the defined reporting period and boundary, exclusion of opinions, future intentions, intellectual property, strategy, other frameworks, and legal compliance. Responsibilities of the Company (preparing the BRSR Report and ensuring data quality) and DNV (providing an independent opinion to management and stakeholders, disclaiming liability) are stated. The document includes DNV contact details, statement number, and signatures of the assurance team.

nodes.title: Assurance Limitations and Company Responsibilities in BRSR Reporting
nodes.summary: The page outlines DNV's assurance engagement, including interviews with senior managers and verification against the Principle of Completeness. It details inherent limitations: data assumed to be provided in good faith, a ±5% materiality threshold, exclusion of financial data assessment (relying on audited financial reports), limited scope to the reporting period and defined boundary, exclusion of opinions, future intentions, intellectual property, strategy, and other frameworks, and no review of legal compliance. Finally, it states Eicher's responsibility for preparing the BRSR Report, ensuring data quality, and maintaining website integrity.

It presents Annexure I, a BRSR Core verified data table covering GHG emissions, water and energy footprints, waste management and circularity, employee wellbeing and safety, gender diversity, inclusive development, and fair customer/supplier engagement, with specific FY 2024-25 values. nodes.title: (iii) The capital investment on energy conservation equipment
nodes.summary: The text details Eicher Motors' capital investment of 4.79 Crores in energy conservation equipment and technology absorption efforts. Engine development upgrades across all models include OBD2B compliance, O2 sensors, high OSC catalysts, and ignition timing automation. Specific engines (350, 440, 450, 650) feature enhancements like flex-fuel oil, vanadium-coated pins, isolated cam covers, balancer cush gears, stainless steel passivation, reversal detection logic, and exhaust/ NVH improvements. Computer-Aided Engineering advancements cover methodologies for dust entry prediction, muffler transmission loss, oil cooler performance, portflow analysis, wheel spoke preload, buckling load calculation, MBD simulation, injection molding, gear whine analysis, road load data analysis, noise source separation, and powertrain noise identification.

nodes.title: Vehicle Development
nodes.summary: The text details vehicle development updates across three engine platforms. For 350 CC vehicles, it covers robustness enhancements like a sealed fuel pump for flex fuel, aluminum alloy rims, clutch and suspension improvements, material additives for UV and ozone resistance, white wall tires, bobber-style components, plastic replacement, brake noise reduction, and flex fuel-specific features. The 450 CC platform includes UV additives, a new fuel cap, improved suspension adjuster, and vibration-reducing control plate. The 650 CC platform features steering stem locknut design, chromed wheel hubs, UV additives, improved clutch cable routing, and big piston USD forks.

nodes.title: Electrical & Electronics Development:
nodes.summary: The text details electrical and electronics developments for various Royal Enfield motorcycle models, including Guerrilla 450, Classic 350 & Goan Classic, Hunter, Interceptor Bear 650, Classic 650, and Scram 440. It lists features such as ride-by-wire throttle, rider modes, TFT dashboards with WiFi navigation, LED lighting, USB Type-C ports, over-the-air updates, gear indication, and telematics. It also covers the RE Wingman telematics system, a Bluetooth diagnostic tool, and flex fuel emission testing capability. R&D expenditure is reported as revenue and capital. Testing and validation achievements include a new cat durability test facility and NABL accreditation for a SHED chamber.

nodes.title: Impact Assessment 1:
nodes.summary: The impact assessment by Sambodhi evaluates a CSR initiative in Tamil Nadu, implemented by the Company with the Madhi Foundation to enhance government school education. Activity A, Strengthening Primary Learning (Ennum Ezhuthum), aimed to improve foundational literacy and numeracy for classes 1-3 by 2025 through level-based instruction, technology, and teacher training. Findings show 75% of teachers reported improved student learning, though more parental engagement is needed. Activity B, Sandbox Schools, transformed teaching and administration in select schools via micro-innovations, with 100% of teachers noting literacy and numeracy growth and 80% receiving monthly training. These schools pilot interventions for scaling, and FLN Vizhas carnivals engaged parents to promote home learning.

nodes.title: Impact Assessment 2:
nodes.summary: The text outlines an impact assessment of a CSR healthcare initiative by Eicher Motors Limited, implemented with Ekam Foundation in Tamil Nadu. It covers the donation of life-saving medical equipment to Chengalpattu Medical College Hospital's Obstetric, Paediatric, and Newborn Departments, and community interventions in four Kancheepuram panchayats. Findings show improved antenatal/postnatal care access, 100% beneficiary awareness of safe motherhood practices, 63% improved diet diversity among postnatal women, 100% adolescent girls' awareness of anemia and improved iron-rich food consumption, and youth volunteers as key health information sources. It notes sustained behavioral change as a challenge, requiring continued education and mobilization.

nodes.title: Impact Assessment 3:
nodes.summary: The text describes an impact assessment of a CSR initiative by CARE India in Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu, aimed at women's economic empowerment. It covers the project's goal to support 200 women entrepreneurs through SEED Centres providing training, mentorship, and resources for micro-enterprises, and mobilizing women into collectives. Findings include: over 70% of participants secured employment or self-employment, 62.5% took leadership roles in SHGs, 36% started individual enterprises with 82% seeing increased income, and improved financial literacy and household incomes. It notes challenges in long-term job retention and career progression, requiring ongoing support, mentorship, and market linkages.
