nodes.title: Revenue Recognition Policies: Variable Consideration, Financing, Warranties, Receivables
nodes.summary: The page outlines revenue recognition policies for domestic and export sales, credit periods, and separate performance obligations like warranties and free service coupons. It covers variable consideration, including estimates, constraints, and refund liabilities for returns; significant financing component with practical expedient for short-term advances; warranty obligations, distinguishing assurance-type (Ind AS 37) and service-type warranties, with allocation of transaction price and revenue recognition; and trade receivables as unconditional rights to consideration, referencing financial instruments policies.

nodes.title: Contract liabilities
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for contract liabilities, revenue recognition for dividends and interest, and leases. It defines contract liabilities as obligations to transfer goods/services after consideration is received, recognized as revenue upon performance. Dividend income is recognized when the right to receive payment is established; interest income when probable and measurable, accrued using the effective interest rate. Lease accounting includes assessing contracts for leases, lessee recognition of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities, measurement at present value of lease payments using incremental borrowing rate, depreciation over shorter of lease term or useful life, and remeasurement upon modifications or changes in lease terms or payments.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies: Income Recognition and Lease Accounting
nodes.summary: The page outlines accounting policies from Eicher Motors' standalone financial statements. It covers revenue recognition for dividends (when the right to receive is established) and interest (accrued on a time basis using the effective interest rate). It also details lease accounting, including the definition of a lease, and the lessee approach for recognizing lease liabilities and right-of-use assets. Right-of-use assets are initially measured at cost, depreciated on a straight-line basis over the shorter of the lease term or useful life (with specified ranges for buildings and land), adjusted for remeasurements, and subject to impairment.

nodes.title: Lease Liabilities
nodes.summary: The text details lease liability recognition at commencement date, measured at present value of lease payments, including fixed payments less incentives, variable payments tied to an index or rate, residual value guarantees, purchase option exercise prices, and termination penalties. Variable payments not tied to an index or rate are expensed when triggered, unless for inventory production. Present value uses the incremental borrowing rate since the implicit rate is often indeterminable. After commencement, lease liabilities increase with interest accretion and decrease with payments, and are remeasured for modifications, changes in lease term, lease payments, or purchase option assessment.

nodes.title: Short-term leases and leases of low-value assets
nodes.summary: This section covers accounting policies for short-term leases and low-value asset leases, including lessor accounting for finance and operating leases, foreign currency translation, borrowing costs, and government grants. It details employee benefits: provident fund (defined benefit and contribution schemes), gratuity (defined benefit plan with actuarial valuation and OCI re-measurements), and other short-term and long-term benefits. Share-based payments (equity-settled, fair value at grant date, expense over vesting, diluted EPS impact) and taxation (current and deferred tax, recognition in P&L, OCI, or equity) are addressed. Intangible assets (recognition, amortization over 3-10 years, derecognition, internally generated criteria), impairment of non-financial assets, inventories, and provisions (warranties, onerous contracts, contingent liabilities) are explained. Financial instruments are covered extensively: classification and measurement (amortized cost, FVTOCI, FVTPL), effective interest method, expected credit loss impairment, derecognition, liability vs equity classification, derivative recognition, and reclassification rules. Cash equivalents, dividends, EPS, investments in subsidiaries/joint ventures (cost less impairment), impairment of investments, events after the reporting period, and new/amended standards (Ind AS 117, Ind AS 116 amendments) are also included.

nodes.title: As a lessor
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies: short-term leases and low-value asset leases (recognition exemption, straight-line expense), lessor accounting for finance and operating leases (classification, income recognition, initial direct costs, contingent rents, net investment measurement, lease payments, manufacturer/dealer lessor profit recognition, subsequent measurement, impairment), foreign currencies (translation of monetary/non-monetary items, exchange differences, net investment in foreign operations, tax effects), borrowing costs (capitalization for qualifying assets, expensing others), and government grants (recognition conditions, expense/asset-related grants, non-monetary grants, EPCG grants, below-market loans).

nodes.title: Provident fund
nodes.summary: The text details the Company's two provident fund schemes. (i) A defined benefit plan for eligible employees, where both contribute monthly a specified percentage of salary, with part of the Company's contribution going to the Eicher Executive Provident Fund Trust. Interest is government-administered, and the Company must cover any shortfall between trust investment returns and the notified rate. The cost is determined using the projected unit credit method with actuarial valuations at each balance sheet date. (ii) A defined contribution scheme for employees not covered under (i), where their portion goes to the government-administered provident fund. The Company has no obligation beyond the contribution payable, which is recognized as expenditure when the employee renders the service.

nodes.title: Gratuity
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for employee benefits and taxation. It details the defined benefit gratuity plan, including contributions, projected unit credit method, actuarial valuations, re-measurements in OCI, and cost categorization (service cost, net interest). It also addresses short-term and other long-term employee benefits, measuring liabilities at undiscounted or present value. Share-based payment arrangements are explained, covering equity-settled transactions, fair value measurement, expense recognition over vesting period, and diluted EPS impact. Finally, taxation is discussed, including current tax based on taxable profit and deferred tax using the liability method on temporary differences.

nodes.title: Employee Benefits, Share-Based Payments, and Taxation Accounting Policies
key_items: Short-term and other long-term employee benefits
nodes.summary: Defines net interest calculation and presentation of defined benefit costs. Covers recognition and measurement of short-term and other long-term employee benefits, with actuarial gains/losses immediately recognized. Details equity-settled share-based payment arrangements, including fair value measurement at grant date, expense recognition over vesting period, SBP reserves, and diluted EPS impact. Explains income tax expense comprising current and deferred tax. Current tax based on taxable profit using enacted rates, with items outside profit or loss recognized in OCI or equity and periodic evaluation of uncertain tax positions. Deferred tax provided using liability method on temporary differences.

nodes.title: Deferred tax
nodes.summary: These notes to Eicher Motors' standalone financial statements cover employee benefits and taxation. For defined benefit plans, net interest is calculated using the discount rate on net liability/asset; the first two components of defined benefit costs are presented in profit or loss as employee benefits expense, and the balance sheet obligation reflects the actual deficit or surplus, with any surplus limited to available economic benefits. Short-term employee benefits are measured at undiscounted amounts; other long-term benefits like annual and sick leave are measured at present value using the projected unit credit method, with actuarial gains/losses immediately recognized in profit or loss. Equity-settled share-based payments are measured at fair value at grant date, recognized with a corresponding increase in SBP reserves over the vesting period, with cumulative expense adjusted to vesting estimates and dilutive effect reflected in diluted EPS. Taxation covers current tax based on taxable profit using enacted rates, with current tax on items outside profit or loss recognized in OCI or equity; deferred tax is provided using the liability method on temporary differences, with exceptions for initial recognition of goodwill/non-business combination transactions and investments in subsidiaries/associates/joint ventures where reversal timing is controlled or probable not to reverse, and deferred tax assets recognized to the extent probable taxable profit exists, reviewed at each reporting period, measured at expected tax rates.

nodes.title: Current and deferred tax for the year
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies: current and deferred tax recognition in profit or loss, other comprehensive income, or equity, with offsetting criteria; GST/value added tax treatment for expenses and assets, including non-recoverable tax and net presentation; property, plant and equipment measured at cost less depreciation and impairment, including capital work in progress, depreciation methods and useful lives, derecognition, and deemed cost transition; intangible assets including separately acquired and internally generated, research and development expenditure, recognition criteria, amortization over 3-10 years, and derecognition; and impairment of non-financial assets assessed at each reporting period with recoverable amount as higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use.

nodes.title: Intangible Assets: Recognition, Amortization, and Derecognition Policies
nodes.summary: The page outlines accounting policies for intangible assets. It covers separately acquired intangible assets, including finite and indefinite useful lives, amortization on a straight-line basis, impairment testing, and annual review of useful life and amortization method. Internally generated intangible assets are discussed, with research expenditure expensed and development expenditure recognized only if recognition criteria are met. Subsequent measurement at cost less amortization and impairment is applied. Derecognition of intangible assets is explained, including disposal, no future economic benefits, and recognition of gains or losses in profit or loss. Development recognition criteria listed include technical feasibility, intention, ability, and probable future economic benefits.

nodes.title: Useful lives of intangible assets
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for intangible assets, impairment of non-financial assets, inventories, and provisions. Intangible assets (product designs, prototypes, software) are amortized over 3-10 years, with software over 3 years or less; useful lives are tabulated. Internally generated intangible assets require technical/financial resources and reliable expenditure measurement. Impairment testing occurs at each reporting period if indicators exist or annually for certain assets, using recoverable amount (higher of fair value less disposal costs and value in use). Cash-generating units are used when individual asset recoverable amount is not estimable; corporate assets are allocated. Value in use uses pre-tax discount rate; fair value less disposal costs uses market transactions or valuation models. Impairment losses are recognized in profit or loss and can be reversed only up to prior carrying amount. Intangible assets not yet available for use are tested annually. Inventories are at lower of cost (moving average) and net realizable value, including raw materials, WIP, finished goods, etc. Provisions are recognized for present obligations from past events when probable and reliably estimable, measured at best estimate with present value if material.

nodes.title: Warranties
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies: product warranties (liability recorded at sale, estimated from historical data and management estimates, annually revised), onerous contracts (unavoidable costs exceeding benefits, provision recognized at lower of fulfillment cost or exit penalties), contingent liabilities (disclosed when possible obligation or present obligation not probable, no disclosure if remote, reviewed at each balance sheet date), financial instruments (definition, recognition when party to contract, initial measurement at fair value with transaction costs adjustments except for fair value through profit or loss items and certain trade receivables), and financial assets (subsequent measurement at amortized cost or fair value through P&L or OCI based on classification, with detailed conditions for amortized cost and FVTOCI for debt instruments including business model and SPPI criteria, and recognition of interest income, impairment, and fair value changes).

nodes.title: Standalone Financial Statements Notes: Onerous Contracts and Contingent Liabilities
nodes.summary: This page from the standalone financial statements notes (amounts in ₹ crores) covers onerous contracts, defining them as contracts where unavoidable costs exceed expected economic benefits, with unavoidable costs being the lower of fulfillment cost or exit penalties, and requiring recognition of a provision. It also covers contingent liabilities, which are disclosed when a possible or present obligation may but probably will not require resource outflow, with no disclosure if remote, and notes that provisions and contingent liabilities are reviewed at each balance sheet date. It further mentions transaction costs on financial assets/liabilities at fair value through profit or loss are expensed immediately, and that financial assets are subsequently measured at amortised cost, fair value through profit or loss, or fair value through other comprehensive income.

nodes.title: Classification and Measurement of financial assets
nodes.summary: The text covers classification and measurement of financial assets and liabilities under Ind AS. It details initial recognition at fair value with transaction costs, and subsequent measurement of debt instruments at amortised cost (if held to collect contractual cash flows and SPPI) or FVTOCI (if held to collect and sell, and SPPI), with interest and impairment in profit or loss and other fair value changes in OCI. All other financial assets are at FVTPL. It explains the effective interest method for amortised cost and interest income. It covers FVTPL measurement for equity investments and debt instruments not meeting criteria, including designation to eliminate accounting mismatch, with gains/losses in profit or loss. It addresses equity instruments designated at FVOCI, with gains/losses never recycled and dividends in profit or loss. Finally, it describes the expected credit loss model for impairment of financial assets at amortised cost, FVTOCI debt, trade receivables, and financial guarantees.

nodes.title: Financial Instruments: Effective Interest Method and Fair Value Measurement
key_items: Financial assets at fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL)
nodes.summary: The page outlines accounting policies for financial instruments. It describes the effective interest method for calculating amortized cost and allocating interest income for debt instruments, excluding those at FVTPL. It covers financial assets at fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL), including equity investments and debt instruments not meeting amortized cost or FVTOCI criteria, or designated at FVTPL to reduce accounting mismatch. FVTPL assets are measured at fair value with gains/losses in profit or loss, including dividends/interest in other income. It also addresses equity instruments designated at FVTOCI, where gains/losses are never recycled to profit or loss, dividends are recognized as other income when the right is established (unless a recovery of cost), and no impairment assessment is required.

nodes.title: Impairment of financial assets
nodes.summary: The text covers impairment of financial assets using the expected credit loss model for amortised cost assets, FVTOCI debt instruments, trade receivables, contractual cash rights, and financial guarantees not at FVTPL, including lifetime expected credit losses for significant credit risk increases and a practical expedient for trade receivables based on historical loss experience and forward-looking information. It also addresses derecognition of financial assets when contractual cash flows expire or risks and rewards are transferred. Additionally, it details classification of financial liabilities and equity instruments, covering equity instruments, financial liabilities at FVTPL (including held for trading and designated liabilities with own credit risk gains/losses in OCI), amortised cost measurement using the effective interest method, derecognition of financial liabilities, and reclassification rules for financial assets and liabilities. Finally, it briefly mentions derivative instruments, such as forward currency contracts for hedging foreign currency risks.

nodes.title: Financial Instruments: Recognition, Classification, and Derecognition Policies
key_items: Classification as financial liability or equity
Reclassification of financial assets and liabilities
nodes.summary: The page covers accounting policies for financial instruments. It begins with a practical expedient for measuring lifetime expected credit loss on trade receivables. It then addresses derecognition of financial assets when contractual rights expire or risks and rewards are transferred. It explains classification of debt and equity instruments as financial liabilities or equity based on contractual substance. It defines equity instruments as residual interests. For financial liabilities, it details classification at fair value through profit or loss, including held-for-trading and designated liabilities, recognition of gains/losses, and treatment of own credit risk. It also covers subsequent measurement at amortised cost using the effective interest method. It outlines derecognition of financial liabilities when obligations are discharged, cancelled, or expired. Finally, it discusses reclassification rules: no reclassification for equity instruments and financial liabilities after initial recognition, and reclassification for debt instruments only upon a change in business model. The page ends with a section heading for derivative instruments.

nodes.title: Initial recognition and subsequent measurement
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies: derivative recognition at fair value with gains/losses to profit or loss except effective cash flow hedges in OCI; cash equivalents definition and cash flow treatment; dividend liability recognition upon authorization; basic and diluted earnings per share calculation; and investment in subsidiaries and joint ventures accounted at cost less impairment, including definitions of subsidiary, associate, joint venture, and joint control.

nodes.title: Impairment of investments
nodes.summary: The text covers three accounting policy notes: impairment of investments, detailing annual review, recognition of impairment loss in profit and loss, and reversal rules; events after the reporting period, explaining adjustment for adjusting events and disclosure of non-adjusting events; and new and amended standards effective from April 1, 2024, including Ind AS 117 Insurance Contracts (not applicable as no insurance contracts) and amendments to Ind AS 116 Leases for sale and leaseback (no material impact as no such transactions).

nodes.title: Ind AS 117 Insurance Contracts
nodes.summary: These notes to the standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, with amounts in crores, cover two main areas. First, it outlines the Company's policy for events after the reporting period, distinguishing between adjusting events (which lead to adjustments in recognized amounts and updated disclosures) and non-adjusting events (which are only disclosed with an estimate of financial effect or a statement that estimation is impracticable). Second, it addresses new and amended standards, noting that the Company applied certain standards effective April 1, 2024, without early adoption. Specifically, it details the Ministry of Corporate Affairs notification of Ind AS 117, Insurance Contracts, effective April 1, 2024, describing its scope, replacement of Ind AS 104, general model with variable fee and premium allocation approaches, and concludes that its application has no material impact on the Company's separate financial statements since no such insurance contracts exist.

nodes.title: Amendments to Ind AS 116 Leases – Lease Liability in a Sale and Leaseback
nodes.summary: The MCA's Second Amendment Rules 2024 amend Ind AS 116 regarding lease liability in sale and leaseback, specifying measurement to avoid recognizing gain/loss on retained right of use. Effective for annual periods from 1 April 2024, applied retrospectively to transactions after initial Ind AS 116 application. No material impact on the Company's financial statements as it has no such transactions. Text also includes Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 and standalone financial statement notes of Eicher Motors Limited for year ended March 31, 2025, with amounts in ₹ crores.

nodes.title: 4. PROPERTY, PLANT AND EQUIPMENT
nodes.summary: The text presents a detailed Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) schedule, including cost and accumulated depreciation movements for freehold land, buildings, plant and equipment, furniture and fixtures, office equipment, and vehicles from April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2025, with additions, disposals, write-offs, exchange adjustments, and net carrying amounts. It notes the transition to Ind AS using deemed cost, provides cost and net carrying amounts for office equipment (including computers), lists immovable property not held in the Company's name, and discloses PPE secured against a SIPCOT soft loan.

nodes.title: 5. CAPITAL WORK-IN-PROGRESS*
nodes.summary: The text details Capital Work-in-Progress, noting properties held without title deeds since August 2, 2004, acquired through group restructuring with registration steps underway. It provides financial particulars for March 31, 2025 and 2024, including opening balances, additions, capitalised amounts, exchange differences, and closing balances. A breakdown of projects in progress and temporarily suspended by age (less than 1 year to more than 3 years) is given for both years. It states no projects are overdue or exceeded original cost. The total capital work-in-progress comprises plant construction and machinery yet to be installed.

nodes.title: 6. INTANGIBLE ASSETS
nodes.summary: The text presents a financial note on intangible assets, detailing product designs, prototypes, and computer software. It includes a table showing cost, additions, disposals, write-offs, exchange adjustments, and accumulated amortisation for the years ended March 31, 2024, and March 31, 2025, along with carrying amounts. It also notes that on transition to Ind AS, the company elected to continue with the previous GAAP carrying value as deemed cost, and that trademarks with finite useful life are amortised over three years, with no restrictions on title or assets pledged as security.

nodes.title: 7. INTANGIBLE ASSETS UNDER DEVELOPMENT*
key_items: As at March 31, 2025; As at March 31, 2024; Investments in subsidiaries & joint ventures
nodes.summary: The text presents a financial statement note on Intangible Assets Under Development, detailing a reconciliation of opening and closing balances for March 31, 2025 and 2024, including additions, capitalisation, write-offs, and exchange differences. It provides an aging analysis of projects in progress and temporarily suspended across time buckets (less than 1 year to more than 3 years), confirms no overdue or cost-exceeded projects for both years, notes that the assets mainly consist of new product development costs, and references investments in subsidiaries and joint ventures.

nodes.title: 8. INVESTMENT IN EQUITY INSTRUMENTS OF SUBSIDIARY COMPANIES (AT COST)
nodes.summary: The text presents a note on investments in equity instruments of subsidiary companies at cost, comparing non-current unquoted investments as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024. It lists five subsidiaries—Royal Enfield Brasil, North America, Thailand, UK, and Europe B.V.—with details of share quantities, face values, currencies, and investment amounts in crores. The sub-total of investments increased from 352.96 in 2024 to 371.62 in 2025, with the addition of Royal Enfield Europe B.V. The text also references the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 and notes forming part of the standalone financial statements, stating amounts are in crores unless otherwise specified.

nodes.title: 9. INVESTMENT IN EQUITY INSTRUMENTS OF JOINT VENTURE COMPANIES (AT COST)
nodes.summary: This section covers Notes 9 and 15–34 of Eicher Motors Limited's standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It details investments in joint venture equity (cost, impairment, Eicher Group Foundation), other investments (unquoted/quoted equity at FVTPL/FVTOCI, mutual funds, target maturity funds, bonds at amortized cost, fair value details, Stark Future strategic investment), loans and bill discounting, other financial assets (deposits, interest accrued, receivables), inventories (raw materials, work in progress, finished goods, provisions), and trade receivables (related party, credit impairment, ageing, credit terms). It also covers cash and cash equivalents (balances, overdrafts, undrawn facilities, pledged mutual funds, cash flow reconciliation), changes in liabilities from financing activities (lease obligations, SIPCOT soft loan, net cash flows, other adjustments), other bank balances (unpaid dividend, unspent CSR with restrictions), other assets (non-current and current breakdowns including advances, prepaid expenses, government receivables, provisions), and share capital (authorized, issued, subscribed, fully paid equity shares with par value, voting rights, liquidation rights, ESOP, promoters' holdings). Additionally, it includes other equity reserves and retained earnings, other financial liabilities (security deposits, employee dues, capital creditors, unpaid dividend, provision for constructive obligation, others), borrowings (non-current secured soft loans from SIPCOT, current secured bank overdraft facilities, repayment terms, security, no defaults), trade payables (dues to micro and small enterprises, other creditors, related parties, aging schedule, disputed dues, balances with struck-off companies, non-interest bearing terms), provisions (employee benefits, warranties, onerous contracts, movements), deferred tax liabilities (net) with comparative tables and movement schedules, current tax liabilities/non-current tax assets, government grants (deferred revenue, sources, recognition, movement), contract liabilities, other liabilities (deferred revenue, statutory remittances, unspent CSR, others including discounts/incentives), revenue from operations (manufactured/traded goods, service warranties, export incentives, scrap sale, after-sales services, product-wise breakdown, reconciliation, contract balances, revenue recognition policies), other income (interest, dividend, grant income, gains, facilitation income, liability write-backs, profit on asset sales, finance income on leases, exchange gain, other income), cost of raw material and components consumed (reconciliation of inventory, purchases, material cost capitalized, sale of raw materials), purchases of traded goods (accessories and allied products), change in inventories (finished goods, work-in-progress, traded goods), and employee benefits expense (salaries, provident fund, share-based payments, staff welfare). All amounts are in ₹ crores unless stated otherwise.

nodes.title: 9. INVESTMENT IN EQUITY INSTRUMENTS OF JOINT VENTURE COMPANIES (AT COST) (intro)
nodes.summary: The text presents financial statement notes: investments in joint venture equity (cost, impairment, Eicher Group Foundation), other investments (unquoted and quoted equity at FVTPL/FVTOCI, mutual funds, target maturity funds, bonds at amortized cost, fair value details, Stark Future strategic investment), loans and bill discounting, other financial assets (deposits, interest accrued, receivables), inventories (raw materials, work in progress, finished goods, provisions), and trade receivables (related party, credit impairment, ageing schedules, credit terms).

nodes.title: 15. CASH AND CASH EQUIVALENTS
key_items: For the purpose of the statement of cash flows, cash and cash equivalents comprise the following:
Changes in liabilities arising from financing activities
nodes.summary: The text presents financial statement notes: cash and cash equivalents (balances, overdrafts, undrawn facilities, pledged mutual funds, cash flow reconciliation), changes in liabilities from financing activities (lease obligations, SIPCOT soft loan, net cash flows, other adjustments), other bank balances (unpaid dividend, unspent CSR with restrictions), other assets (non-current and current breakdowns including advances, prepaid expenses, government receivables, provisions), and share capital (authorized, issued, subscribed, fully paid equity shares with par value, voting rights, liquidation rights). All amounts are in crores unless stated otherwise.

nodes.title: 18. SHARE CAPITAL
nodes.summary: This note details share capital: equity share capital with authorized (30 crore shares of Re. 1) and issued/subscribed/fully paid-up shares (27.42 crore shares as of March 31, 2025), including reconciliation of shares outstanding (beginning, issued during year, ending), and shareholders holding over 5% (The Simran Siddhartha Tara Benefit Trust with 43.88%). It covers share options under ESOP having no dividend/voting rights. Preference share capital authorized (1,01,000 redeemable preference shares of Rs. 100 each) with none issued. It also lists equity shares held by promoters, showing number of shares at beginning and end of year, percentage of total shares, and changes during the year for both FY 2024-25 and FY 2023-24, with footnotes explaining changes due to ESOP allotments and share transfers.

nodes.title: 19. OTHER EQUITY
nodes.summary: This section presents Note 19, 'Other Equity,' from Eicher Motors Limited's standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, detailing various equity reserves and retained earnings. It includes a summary table of total other equity components for 2025 and 2024, followed by detailed notes on each reserve: capital reserve (static), capital redemption reserve, securities premium, general reserves, share-based payments reserve, foreign currency translation reserve, hedge reserve, debt instruments through OCI, FVTOCI reserve, and retained earnings. Each note provides opening and closing balances, movements during the year, and explanations of the nature and utilization of each reserve, including regulatory requirements and accounting treatments.

nodes.title: A Capital reserve
nodes.summary: The text presents Note 19, 'Other Equity,' from Eicher Motors Limited's standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It includes a table summarizing total other equity components for 2025 and 2024, such as capital reserves, capital redemption reserve, securities premium, general reserves, share-based payments reserve, foreign currency translation reserve, hedge reserve, debt instruments through OCI, FVTOCI reserve, and retained earnings, with totals of 14,867.60 crores and 15,666.20 crores respectively. Detailed notes follow for each reserve: capital reserve (static at 0.25 crores), capital redemption reserve (1.41 crores, usable for bonus shares), securities premium (increased from 319.60 to 434.67 crores via share proceeds and transfers, usable only for limited purposes like bonus shares), general reserves (static at 339.89 crores, created under the erstwhile Companies Act 1956, now optional but usable per Companies Act 2013), and share-based payments reserve (increased from 77.14 to 106.32 crores due to share-based expenses, net of transfers to securities premium), relating to employee share option plans referenced in note 49.

nodes.title: Reserves: Capital Redemption, Securities Premium, and General Reserves
nodes.summary: The page presents notes to the standalone financial statements of Eicher Motors Limited for the year ended March 31, 2025, covering three reserve accounts: Capital Redemption Reserve, Securities Premium, and General Reserves. For each, it provides opening and closing balances for March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024, along with movements during the year. It explains that the Capital Redemption Reserve was created on share buyback and can be used for fully paid bonus shares. Securities Premium records premium on share issues and is utilized for limited purposes like bonus shares under the Companies Act, 2013. General Reserve, created under the erstwhile Companies Act 1956 through annual transfers, now has no mandatory transfer requirement but can be utilized per the Companies Act, 2013.

nodes.title: E Share based payments reserve
nodes.summary: The text presents five equity reserves from standalone financial statements: share-based payments reserve (opening/closing balances, expenses, transfers), foreign currency translation reserve (exchange differences recognized in OCI and reclassified on disposal), hedge reserve (cash flow hedges for foreign currency risk on receivables), debt instruments through OCI reserve (cumulative gains/losses on revaluation), and FVTOCI reserve for equity instruments (fair value changes in OCI). Each includes opening balance, movements, closing balance, and explanatory notes.

nodes.title: Standalone Financial Statement Notes: Reserves
nodes.summary: This page presents notes forming part of the standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, with all amounts in crores. It covers two reserves: F Foreign currency translation reserve, showing opening balance, exchange differences on translation of foreign operations, and closing balance for 2025 and 2024, along with accounting treatment recognizing exchange differences in other comprehensive income and reclassifying cumulative amounts to profit or loss on disposal. G Hedge reserve, showing opening balance, gains/losses on cash flow hedges, and closing balance for both years, with explanation of hedging instruments (foreign currency forward contracts) for foreign currency risk on trade receivables, recognition of effective portion in cash flow hedges, and reclassification to profit and loss when the hedged item affects profit or loss.

nodes.title: H Debt instruments through other comprehensive income
nodes.summary: The text presents financial statement notes on reserves and retained earnings. It details the Debt Instruments through OCI reserve, showing opening balances, other comprehensive income, and closing balances for 2025 and 2024, with a description of its nature. It also covers the FVTOCI reserve for equity instruments, including opening and closing balances and the company's policy. Finally, it provides a table for Retained earnings, detailing opening balance, profit for the year, OCI from remeasurement of defined benefit obligation, dividends paid, total appropriations, and closing balance, along with a description of retained earnings.

nodes.title: 21. BORROWINGS
nodes.summary: The text presents Note 21, Borrowings, detailing non-current secured soft loans from SIPCOT with a subsidized interest rate, repayment terms, and security against property, plant, and equipment, along with current secured bank overdraft facilities, their interest rates, and collateral. It provides comparative figures as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, and states that the Company has not defaulted on any loans or interest payable.

nodes.title: 22. TRADE PAYABLES
key_items: Terms and conditions of the above financial liabilities:
nodes.summary: The text presents Note 22 on Trade Payables, comparing balances as of March 31, 2025 and 2024. It details outstanding dues to micro and small enterprises, other creditors, and related parties, including subtotals. It includes an aging schedule for trade payables, disputed dues, and unbilled/not due amounts for both years. It lists balances with companies struck off under the Companies Act, specifying the company name, transaction nature, relationship, and amounts for 2025/2024 and 2024/2023. nodes.title: 47.1 Capital Management
nodes.summary: The text covers financial instruments, specifically capital management. It outlines the Company's objective to ensure going concern status while maximizing stakeholder returns through efficient capital allocation, working capital optimization, and investment of surplus funds. It notes that operational cash flows and equity meet capital requirements, and the Company is not subject to externally imposed capital requirements. Management regularly reviews the capital structure, considering working capital risks. No changes were made to capital management objectives, policies, or processes during the years ended March 31, 2025 and 2024. It also includes a table with particulars: borrowings less cash and cash equivalents, net debt, share capital, other equity, total equity, and gearing ratio.

nodes.title: 47.2 Categories of financial instruments

nodes.title: 47.3 Fair value measurements
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Company's fair value measurement hierarchy for financial instruments, categorizing them into three levels. Level 1 uses quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities. Level 2 uses observable inputs other than Level 1 quoted prices, either directly or indirectly. Level 3 uses unobservable inputs not based on market data, determined via valuation models with assumptions unsupported by observable market transactions or data.

nodes.title: Quantitative disclosures fair value measurement hierarchy for assets:

It includes notes on equity investments in Flamesun Solar Private Limited and Suryadev Alloys & Power Private Limited, including share purchase agreement terms, and on Stark Future S.L. designated at fair value through OCI. It also provides valuation inputs: valuation methods (comparable transactions multiple, average of discounted cash flow and market approach), weighted average cost of capital/discount rate of 25.0%, long-term growth rate of 2.5%, long-term EBITDA margin of 20.0%, and target multiple of 3.0x for March 31, 2025, with certain inputs not applicable for March 31, 2024.

nodes.title: Employee Stock Option Plan, 2006 of the Company
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Employee Stock Option Plan, 2006 (ESOP 2006) of the Company. Exercise price is set by the Committee at not less than the closing market price on NSE/BSE on the preceding day. Options can be exercised until seven years from vesting, after which they lapse. nodes.summary: The text presents the consolidated cash flow statement's financing activities section, detailing items like working capital loans, soft loans, interest, equity proceeds, lease payments, and dividends, along with net cash flow, exchange differences, and cash reconciliation. It includes the auditor's report and board signatures, corporate information for Eicher Motors Limited, statement of compliance with Ind AS, basis of preparation, and summary of material accounting policies covering consolidation, joint ventures, current/non-current classification, fair value measurement, and revenue recognition.

nodes.title: Sale of manufactured and traded goods
nodes.summary: Revenue from sale of goods is recognized when control transfers to the customer. Domestic sales are recognized at dispatch from the point of sale; export sales on shipment or delivery per terms, initially at transaction-date exchange rates. The Group offers specific credit periods to certain customers. It assesses whether contracts contain separate performance obligations like warranties, Road Side Assistance, or Free Service Coupons, allocating transaction price accordingly. In determining transaction price, the Group considers variable consideration, significant financing components, non-cash consideration, and consideration payable to the customer.

nodes.title: Variable consideration
nodes.summary: The text outlines several accounting policies: variable consideration, including estimates, constraints, rights of return, and refund liabilities; significant financing component using the practical expedient for short-term advances; warranty obligations distinguishing assurance-type (under Ind AS 37) and service-type warranties (treated as separate performance obligations with revenue recognized as costs are incurred); trade receivables as unconditional rights to consideration; contract liabilities for advance payments recognized as revenue upon performance; dividend income recognized when the right to receive is established and interest income using the effective interest method; and leases, including the lessee's single recognition approach, right-of-use assets measured at cost and depreciated over the lease term or useful life, with exceptions for short-term and low-value leases.

nodes.title: Consolidated Financial Statements Notes: Revenue, Receivables, and Leases
nodes.summary: The page covers accounting policies for significant financing component (practical expedient for short-term advances), warranty obligations (assurance-type under Ind AS 37 and service-type as separate performance obligations with revenue recognition), trade receivables (unconditional right to consideration), contract liabilities (obligation to transfer goods/services for received consideration), dividend and interest income (recognition criteria), and leases (lessee accounting with single recognition model, lease liabilities, and right-of-use assets).

nodes.title: i) Right-of-use assets
nodes.summary: The text outlines the accounting policy for right-of-use assets, including recognition at lease commencement, initial measurement at cost (comprising lease liabilities, direct costs, and payments less incentives), subsequent measurement at cost less depreciation and impairment, and adjustment for lease liability remeasurement. Depreciation is straight-line over the shorter of the lease term and useful life (2-20 years for buildings, 99 years for others), or over the asset's useful life if ownership transfers or a purchase option is expected. It also notes that right-of-use assets are subject to impairment under section 3.15.

nodes.title: Lease Liabilities
nodes.summary: The text details the recognition and measurement of lease liabilities at the commencement date, including the components of lease payments (fixed payments, variable payments based on an index or rate, residual value guarantees, purchase option exercise price, and termination penalties). It explains that variable payments not based on an index or rate are expensed when incurred. It also covers the use of the incremental borrowing rate for present value calculation, subsequent accretion of interest, reduction for lease payments, and remeasurement triggers such as lease modifications, changes in lease term, lease payments, or purchase option assessment.

nodes.title: Short-term leases and leases of low-value assets
nodes.summary: The section covers accounting policies for short-term leases and low-value assets, including lessor accounting for finance and operating leases, foreign currency translation, borrowing costs, and government grants. It details employee benefits: provident fund (defined benefit and contribution plans), gratuity (defined benefit plan), and short-term and other long-term benefits. It also covers share-based payments, current and deferred tax (recognition, measurement, uncertain tax positions, offsetting), GST treatment, property, plant and equipment (measurement, depreciation, derecognition), intangible assets (recognition, amortization, impairment, derecognition), impairment of non-financial assets, inventories, provisions, contingent liabilities, and financial instruments (classification, measurement, effective interest method, FVTPL, impairment, derecognition, liability/equity classification, derivatives, cash and cash equivalents, dividends, EPS, joint ventures, impairment of investments, events after reporting period, new standards, and detailed PP&E disclosures).

nodes.title: As a lessor
nodes.summary: The text covers lease accounting for short-term and low-value assets, lessor accounting for finance and operating leases (including manufacturer/dealer lessors), foreign currency translation, borrowing costs, and government grants. It details recognition exemptions, lease classification, income recognition, initial and subsequent measurement of net investments, and treatment of residual value guarantees. Foreign currency policies include translation of monetary and non-monetary items, exchange differences, and net investment hedging. Borrowing costs attributable to qualifying assets are capitalized. Government grants are recognized when reasonable assurance exists, with income recognition tied to related costs or asset useful life, including non-monetary grants and EPCG grants.

nodes.title: Provident fund
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Group's provident fund schemes for employees. It describes a defined benefit plan where both employee and employer contribute monthly, with part going to the Eicher Executive Provident Fund Trust; the Group must cover any shortfall between trust investment returns and the government-notified interest rate. Benefits are determined using the projected unit credit method with actuarial valuations at each balance sheet date. Employees not covered by this scheme are in a defined contribution plan with no Group obligation beyond contributions, which are recognized as expenditure when services are rendered.

nodes.title: Gratuity
nodes.summary:
Gratuity
The Group operates a defined benefit gratuity plan, which requires contributions to be made to a separately administered fund.
Payments to defined contribution plans are recognised as an expense when employees have rendered service entitling them to the contributions.
Net interest is calculated by applying the discount rate to the net defined benefit liability or asset.
The Group presents the first two components of defined benefit costs in profit or loss in the line item ‘Employee benefits expense’.
The retirement benefit obligation recognised in the balance sheet represents the actual deficit or surplus in the Group’s defined benefit plans. Any surplus resulting from this calculation is limited to the present value of any economic benefits available in the form of refunds from the plan or reductions in future contributions to the plans.

nodes.title: Short-term and other long-term employee benefits
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for employee benefits and share-based payments. It details recognition and measurement of short-term benefits at undiscounted amounts, and defined benefit plans using the projected unit credit method with actuarial valuations, immediate recognition of re-measurements in other comprehensive income, and net interest calculation. Other long-term benefits like annual and sick leave are measured at present value with actuarial gains/losses immediately in profit or loss. It also addresses equity-settled share-based payments measured at grant-date fair value, recognized over the vesting period with a corresponding increase in SBP reserves, cumulative expense adjustments, and dilutive effect on earnings per share. Taxation is briefly mentioned as current plus deferred tax.

nodes.title: Current tax
nodes.summary: The text covers current tax and deferred tax accounting. Current tax is based on taxable profit, differing from accounting profit due to permanent and temporary differences, and is calculated using enacted tax rates. Current tax on items outside profit or loss is recognized in OCI or equity. Management evaluates uncertain tax positions and sets provisions. Deferred tax uses the liability method on temporary differences between tax bases and carrying amounts. Deferred tax liabilities are recognized for all taxable temporary differences except goodwill initial recognition and certain investments where reversal is controlled. Deferred tax assets are recognized for deductible temporary differences, unused tax credits, and losses when probable taxable profit exists, with exceptions for initial recognition and certain investments. Deferred tax on outside-profit-or-loss items is recognized in OCI or equity.

nodes.title: Deferred tax
nodes.summary: These notes from Eicher Motors' consolidated financial statements cover accounting for share-based payments, including expense recognition over vesting periods, cumulative expense adjustments, and dilution impact on earnings per share. They also detail taxation: current tax based on taxable profit, recognition outside profit or loss, and management evaluation of uncertain tax positions; deferred tax using the liability method on temporary differences, with exceptions for goodwill, initial recognition, and investments in subsidiaries/associates/joint ventures; recognition of deferred tax assets limited to probable taxable profit; periodic review and reduction of deferred tax asset carrying amounts; measurement at expected enacted tax rates; and reflection of expected recovery or settlement of asset/liability carrying amounts.

nodes.title: Current and deferred tax for the year
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for current and deferred tax, including recognition in profit or loss or other comprehensive income/equity, and offsetting conditions. It details GST/value added tax treatment on assets and expenses, including non-recoverable tax and net tax presentation. It then addresses property, plant and equipment: measurement at cost less depreciation and impairment, cost components, separate depreciation of significant parts, non-depreciation of freehold land, capital work in progress, depreciation methods and useful lives (including moulds and dies), review of estimates, pro-rata depreciation, derecognition, and disclosure of useful lives. It also mentions deemed cost transition and introduces intangible assets.

nodes.title: Intangible assets acquired separately
nodes.summary: The text details accounting policies for intangible assets. Separately acquired finite-life assets are carried at cost less amortisation and impairment, amortised straight-line, and reviewed annually. Indefinite-life assets are not amortised but tested annually for impairment. Internally generated assets: research expenditure is expensed; development expenditure is capitalised only if six criteria (technical feasibility, intention, ability, future benefits, resources, reliable measurement) are met, from the date criteria are met. Otherwise, development is expensed. Capitalised internally generated assets are subsequently carried at cost less amortisation and impairment, like separately acquired assets.

nodes.title: De-recognition of intangible assets
nodes.summary:
De-recognition of intangible assets
An intangible asset is de-recognised on disposal, or when no future economic benefits are expected from use or disposal. Gains or losses arising from de-recognition of an intangible asset, measured as the difference between the net disposal proceeds and the carrying amount of the asset, and are recognised in the statement of profit or loss when the asset is de-recognised.

nodes.title: Useful lives of intangible assets
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies: intangible asset useful lives (product designs/prototypes 3-10 years, software 3 years) and amortization; impairment of non-financial assets, including annual testing, recoverable amount determination (higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use), cash-generating unit allocation, discounting future cash flows, impairment loss recognition and reversal; inventories measured at lower of cost (moving average) and net realizable value, including cost components; provisions recognized for present obligations, including onerous contracts and warranties, with annual review; contingent liabilities disclosure based on probability of outflow; and financial instruments, covering initial recognition at fair value, transaction costs, and subsequent measurement of financial assets at amortized cost, fair value through profit or loss, or fair value through other comprehensive income.

nodes.title: Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Financial Instruments Notes
nodes.summary: This page from Eicher Motors' consolidated financial statements covers inventory cost basis, then provisions including recognition criteria, measurement, onerous contracts, warranties, and contingent liabilities. It also addresses financial instruments: definition, recognition, initial measurement at fair value with transaction cost adjustments, and subsequent measurement of financial assets at amortised cost, fair value through profit or loss, or fair value through other comprehensive income.

nodes.title: Classification and Measurement of financial assets
nodes.summary: The text details classification and measurement of financial assets, specifically debt instruments. It outlines two categories: amortised cost, where the business model aims to collect contractual cash flows and terms are solely payments of principal and interest (SPPI); and fair value through other comprehensive income (FVTOCI), where the business model collects cash flows and sells assets, with SPPI terms. Interest income and impairment are recognized in profit or loss for FVTOCI, while remaining fair value changes go to OCI, reclassified to profit or loss on de-recognition. All other financial assets are measured at fair value through profit or loss.

nodes.title: Effective interest method
nodes.summary:
Effective interest method
The effective interest method is a method of calculating the amortised cost of a debt instrument and of allocating interest income over the relevant period. The effective interest rate is the rate that exactly discounts estimated future cash receipts (including all fees and points paid or received that form an integral part of the effective interest rate, transaction costs and other premiums or discounts) through the expected life of the debt instrument, or, where appropriate, a shorter period, to the net carrying amount on initial recognition.
Income is recognised on an effective interest basis for debt instruments other than those financial assets classified at FVTPL. Interest income is recognised in profit or loss and is included in the “Other income” line item.

nodes.title: Financial assets at fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL)
nodes.summary: The text details accounting policies for financial assets and liabilities. It covers classification and measurement of financial assets at FVTPL, including equity and debt instruments, designation criteria, and recognition of gains, losses, and dividends. It also addresses equity instruments designated at FVOCI, impairment using the expected credit loss model, and de-recognition of financial assets. For financial liabilities and equity instruments, it explains classification as liability or equity, accounting for financial liabilities at FVTPL (including own credit risk treatment) and at amortised cost using the effective interest method, and recognition of related gains, losses, and interest expense.

nodes.title: Financial Instruments: Impairment, Derecognition, Liability/Equity Classification
key_items: Classification as financial liability or equity
nodes.summary: The page covers accounting policies for financial instruments under Ind AS 32 and 109. It addresses equity instruments designated at FVOCI, including gain/loss treatment and dividend recognition. It details the expected credit loss model for impairment of financial assets, covering scope, significant credit risk increase, and practical expedient for trade receivables. De-recognition of financial assets is explained based on expiration of contractual rights or transfer of risks and rewards. It also covers classification of financial liabilities versus equity instruments, defining equity instruments as residual interests. Finally, it discusses financial liabilities at FVTPL, including held-for-trading and designated liabilities, recognition of gains/losses, own credit risk treatment in OCI, and amortized cost measurement using the effective interest method.

nodes.title: Financial liabilities
nodes.summary: These consolidated financial statement notes for Eicher Motors Limited cover accounting policies for financial instruments under Ind AS. They detail classification and measurement of financial assets, including equity instruments at FVOCI and impairment using the expected credit loss model. Financial liabilities and equity instruments are classified by substance, with policies on FVTPL liabilities and the effective interest method. De-recognition and reclassification rules for financial assets and liabilities are provided. Derivative instruments, particularly forward currency contracts for hedging, are addressed. Cash and cash equivalents are defined, along with dividend recognition and earnings per share calculations. Finally, accounting for investments in joint ventures at cost less impairment is specified.

nodes.title: Financial Liabilities De-recognition and Asset Reclassification Policies
key_items: Reclassification of financial assets and liabilities
nodes.summary: This page from the consolidated financial statements notes covers de-recognition of financial liabilities, stating they are removed when obligations are discharged, cancelled, or expired. It also addresses reclassification of financial assets and liabilities: classification is determined at initial recognition; no reclassification for equity instruments and financial liabilities; debt instruments are reclassified only upon a change in business model, which is expected to be infrequent and determined by senior management due to significant external or internal changes. The page also begins a section on derivative instruments.

nodes.title: Initial recognition and subsequent measurement
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies: derivative instruments are initially recognized at fair value and subsequently remeasured, with gains/losses to profit or loss except effective cash flow hedges in OCI; cash and cash equivalents include cash at banks, on hand, and short-term deposits with original maturity of three months or less, net of overdrafts for cash flow purposes; dividend liability is recognized when authorized and no longer discretionary, with interim dividends declared by the Board and corresponding amount in other equity; basic EPS is profit after tax divided by weighted average equity shares, diluted EPS adjusts profit and shares for dilutive potential equity shares; investments in joint ventures are accounted at cost less impairment, with joint control requiring unanimous consent.
