It details 'Other Income' including interest, grants, fair value gains, and other non-operating items; 'Cost of Raw Material and Components Consumed' showing inventory changes, purchases, and adjustments; 'Purchases of Traded Goods' for accessories; 'Change in Inventories' of finished goods, work-in-progress, and traded goods; and 'Employee Benefits Expense' covering salaries, provident fund, share-based payments, and staff welfare, all with corresponding amounts for both years.

nodes.title: Notes on Cost of Materials, Purchases of Traded Goods, and Inventory Changes
key_items: 30. COST OF RAW MATERIAL AND COMPONENTS CONSUMED
32. CHANGE IN INVENTORIES OF FINISHED GOODS, WORK-IN-PROGRESS AND TRADED GOODS
nodes.summary: This page presents three notes to the consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025: Note 30 details the cost of raw materials and components consumed, showing beginning and ending inventories, purchases, deductions for capitalized vehicle material costs and raw material sales to suppliers, with a capital work-in-progress inclusion; Note 31 lists purchases of traded goods, specifically accessories and allied products, for current and prior years; Note 32 reports the change in inventories of finished goods, work-in-progress, and traded goods, providing opening and closing balances and the resulting increase or decrease for each category. All amounts are in crores unless stated otherwise.

nodes.title: 33. EMPLOYEE BENEFITS EXPENSE
nodes.summary: The text presents notes from Eicher Motors Limited's consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, covering employee benefits expense, finance costs, depreciation and amortisation expense, and other expenses. Employee benefits include salaries, provident fund contributions, share-based payments, and staff welfare, with comparative figures for 2024 and references to gratuity and share-based payment notes. It also mentions the Code on Social Security, 2020, noting partial implementation. Finance costs detail interest on bills, borrowings, provisions, and lease liabilities. Depreciation covers property, plant, equipment, intangibles, and right-of-use assets. Other expenses list various items such as stores consumption, asset sale losses, power, insurance, repairs, rates, advertisement, freight, warranty provisions, lease expenses, legal fees, travel, development, CSR, and receivables provisions, with corresponding amounts for both years.

nodes.title: Finance Costs and Depreciation Notes from Eicher Motors Consolidated Statements
nodes.summary: This page from Eicher Motors Limited's consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, presents two notes: Finance Costs and Depreciation and Amortisation Expense. It also includes a brief update on the Code on Social Security, 2020, noting that certain sections are effective but final rules are pending. Note 34, Finance Costs, lists interest expense on bills discounting, borrowings, unwinding of discount on provisions, and interest on lease liabilities, with a total. Note 35, Depreciation and Amortisation Expense, details depreciation on property, plant and equipment, amortisation of intangible assets, and depreciation of right-of-use assets, with a total. All amounts are in crores unless stated otherwise.

nodes.title: 36. OTHER EXPENSES
nodes.summary: The text presents Note 36, "Other Expenses," from consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, with comparatives for 2024. It lists expense particulars in ₹ crores: stores and machinery spares, loss on asset sales, power and fuel, insurance, repairs and maintenance (buildings, plant, others), rates and taxes, advertisement, freight and handling, warranty and onerous contract provisions, selling and distribution expenses, short-term lease expenses, legal and professional charges, travelling, development, CSR expenditure, credit-impaired receivables provision, and miscellaneous expenses, with totals. A footnote details auditor payments (excluding GST) for audit, limited reviews, other services, and expense reimbursement, with amounts for both years and subtotals.

nodes.title: 37. INCOME TAX RECOGNIZED IN STATEMENT OF PROFIT AND LOSS
nodes.summary: The text presents income tax disclosures for the years ended March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024. It details current and deferred tax components, totaling income tax expense recognized in profit and loss, and provides a reconciliation of income tax expense to accounting profit, including adjustments for long-term capital gains, ESOP/RSU expenses, fair valuation changes, deferred tax assets on subsidiary losses, joint venture profit share, CSR expenses, and others. The applicable tax rate computation is shown (basic rate 22%, surcharge 10%, cess 4%, totaling 25.168%). It also reports deferred tax charges/(benefits) recognized in other comprehensive income, bifurcated into items that will be reclassified to profit or loss and items that will not.

nodes.title: 38. CRITICAL ACCOUNTING JUDGEMENT AND KEY SOURCES OF ESTIMATION UNCERTAINTY
nodes.summary: This note addresses critical accounting judgments and estimation uncertainties. It covers management's required judgments, estimates, and assumptions about asset and liability carrying amounts, noting estimates are based on historical experience and reviewed ongoing, with revisions recognized in the relevant periods. Specific areas include: control over VE Commercial Vehicles Limited, classified as a joint venture under Ind AS 111 due to joint control despite EML's 54.4% stake; recoverability of intangible assets and those under development, including capitalization criteria and impairment indicators; useful lives of depreciable assets, reviewed at each reporting date; share-based payments, requiring valuation model and input assumptions; impairment of non-financial assets, based on recoverable amount calculations; and equity investments designated at FVTOCI, including Stark Future S.L., with fair value changes recognized in OCI.

nodes.title: 39. RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT COSTS:
nodes.summary: The text presents four financial notes: (39) Research and development costs for FY2025, detailing capitalized amounts (₹463.08 crores vs. ₹314.69 crores prior year) and expensed non-capitalizable costs (₹149.64 crores vs. ₹148.98 crores). (40) Contingent liabilities not provided for, covering excise, sales tax, service tax, customs, GST, direct tax matters, claims against the Group, guarantees, and joint venture liabilities, with management noting no material impact expected. (41) Dues to micro and small enterprises under MSMED Act, showing principal unpaid, interest due, payments beyond appointed day, and accrued interest. (42) Employee benefit plans, specifically defined contribution plans (provident fund, superannuation, ESIC, other funds) with expense details and capitalization notes.

nodes.title: Contingent Liabilities and MSMED Dues Disclosures
key_items: 41. DETAILS OF DUES TO MICRO AND SMALL ENTERPRISES AS DEFINED UNDER THE MSMED ACT, 2006
Particulars; For the year ended March 31, 2024
nodes.summary: The page presents two notes from Eicher Motors' consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. Note 40 details contingent liabilities not provided for, comparing March 31, 2025 and 2024 figures across categories: excise, sales tax, service tax, customs duty, GST, and direct tax matters; claims against the Group not acknowledged as debts; guarantees to banks/others; and liabilities from interests in a joint venture. It notes legal proceedings are ongoing and management expects no material impact. Note 41 discloses dues to micro and small enterprises under the MSMED Act, 2006, showing unpaid principal, interest due and unpaid, payments beyond appointed days, interest due and payable, accrued unpaid interest, and further interest payable in succeeding years for both years.

nodes.title: 42. EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS
nodes.summary: The text details employee benefit plans, including defined contribution plans (provident fund, superannuation, ESIC, other funds) with expenses and capitalized amounts. It covers defined benefit plans (gratuity and provident fund) discussing actuarial risks (investment, interest, longevity, salary), actuarial valuation by Mr. K.K. Dharni, and principal assumptions (discount rate, salary increase, retirement age, withdrawal rate, mortality). It presents amounts recognized in profit and loss, remeasurements in OCI, balance sheet obligations, movements in defined benefit obligation and plan assets, fair value of plan assets by category, sensitivity analysis for changes in discount rate and salary growth, maturity profile, and expected contributions for future years.

nodes.title: 43. EARNINGS PER SHARE
key_items: Basic earnings per share (in `) Diluted earnings per share (in `) Basic earnings per share
nodes.summary: The text presents earnings per share (EPS) data for the years ended March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, including basic and diluted EPS in rupees. It details the net profit and weighted average number of equity shares used for basic EPS calculations for both years. For diluted EPS, it further includes shares deemed issued for no consideration under employee stock option and restricted stock unit plans, along with the adjusted weighted average shares. All amounts are in crores unless stated otherwise, and the note is part of the consolidated financial statements.

nodes.title: 44. SEGMENT REPORTING DISCLOSURE
nodes.summary: The text discusses segment reporting disclosure under Ind AS 108, noting the Group operates as a single automotive segment without separate reportable segments. It provides geographical information split into domestic (India) and overseas segments, including revenue from operations and non-current segment assets for the years ended March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024. Definitions clarify that domestic and overseas segments cover sales/services to customers in and outside India, non-current segment assets exclude non-current financial assets, and accounting policies align with the Group's policies. It also states that no customer individually accounted for more than 10% of revenue.

nodes.title: 45. RELATED PARTY DISCLOSURES UNDER IND AS 24
key_items: d. Transactions with the related parties
e. Balance outstanding at the year end
nodes.summary: This note discloses related party information under IND AS 24 for Eicher Motors Limited's consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It lists related parties by name, relationship (joint ventures, subsidiaries, entities under key management personnel control, post-employment benefit plans, and other related entities), and principal place of business. It also details key management personnel and their roles. Transactions with key management personnel include remuneration, short-term benefits, post-employment benefits, share-based payments, sitting fees, and commission for both years. Transactions with other related parties cover purchases, services, brand fees, CSR contributions, fund contributions, sales, and legal charges. Balance outstanding at year-end includes trade payables, advances, bills discounted, security deposits, rent payable, and commission payable. Terms and conditions state transactions are at arm's length, unsecured, interest-free, and settled in cash.

nodes.title: 46. FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS
nodes.summary: The text covers financial instruments disclosures in consolidated financial statements. It details capital management objectives, policies, and gearing ratios for 2025 and 2024, noting no externally imposed capital requirements and no breaches in financial covenants. It categorizes financial instruments by measurement basis (fair value through P&L, OCI, amortized cost) with carrying amounts as of March 31, 2025 and 2024. Fair value measurements are explained using a three-level hierarchy, with quantitative disclosures for assets, valuation methods for unquoted equity, and fair values of bonds. It also discusses methods and assumptions for estimating fair values, noting no transfers between hierarchy levels.

nodes.title: 47. FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT OBJECTIVES AND POLICIES
nodes.summary: The text covers the Group's financial risk management objectives and policies, including market risk (currency, interest rate, other price risk), credit risk, and liquidity risk. It details foreign currency exposure and sensitivity analysis, credit risk management with impairment allowance movement, NAV price sensitivity, interest rate risk insignificance, and liquidity risk management with maturity profiles of financial liabilities.

nodes.title: 48. SHARE-BASED PAYMENTS
nodes.summary: This section covers the company's share-based payment plans, specifically the Employee Stock Option Plan, 2006 (ESOP 2006) and the Restricted Stock Units Plan, 2019 (RSU 2019). For each plan, it details approval dates, administration by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, eligibility criteria, vesting conditions, exercise price and period, payment methods, conversion to equity shares, and rights until exercise. It also provides detailed disclosures including option series, grant dates, number of options, vesting periods, expiry dates, exercise prices, fair values, valuation methodology using Black-Scholes, assumptions, movements in options during the year, effect on profit or loss, options exercised, and options outstanding at year-end with remaining contractual life, for the year ended March 31, 2025.

nodes.title: Employee Stock Option Plan, 2006 of the Company
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Employee Stock Option Plan, 2006 (ESOP, 2006), approved by shareholders on July 5, 2006, and administered by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee. It covers eligibility (permanent full-time employees, excluding promoters and promoter group, per SEBI Regulations), vesting conditions (minimum one year, continuous employment), exercise price (not less than closing market price on NSE/BSE preceding grant date), exercise period (up to seven years from vesting, lapsing thereafter), payment of exercise price as approved, conversion into one equity share per option, no payment on grant, and no dividend or voting rights until exercise. The document is part of the consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, with amounts in crores.

nodes.title: Details of the Employee Stock Option Plan, 2006 of the Company
nodes.summary: The text details the Employee Stock Option Plan, 2006, listing option series with grant dates, number of options, vesting periods, expiry dates, exercise prices, and fair values. It includes weighted average fair value of options granted, valuation methodology using Black-Scholes, and assumptions like volatility, dividend yield, and risk-free rate. Movements in options during the year (beginning balance, granted, forfeited, exercised, ending balance, exercisable) are provided for both current and previous years, along with the effect on profit or loss. Details of options exercised during the year and previous year, including series, number, exercise date, and price, are given. Finally, options outstanding at year-end with remaining contractual life and exercise price are summarized.

nodes.title: Restricted Stock Units Plan, 2019 ("RSU 2019")
nodes.summary: The text describes the Eicher Motors Limited Restricted Stock Units Plan 2019 (RSU 2019), approved by shareholders on August 1, 2019, and formulated by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee under SEBI Regulations 2021. It covers eligibility (permanent employees, directors, subsidiary employees), committee's role in determining eligibility and vesting criteria based on continued employment and/or performance. Vesting period is between one and seven years from grant. Exercise price is face value at exercise; exercise period is up to seven years from vesting, after which RSUs lapse. Payment methods for exercise price are approved by the committee. Each RSU converts to one equity share; no payment on grant; no dividend or voting rights until conversion. It also includes financial statement notes for the year ended March 31, 2025.

nodes.title: Detail of Restricted Stock Units Plan, 2019 ("RSU 2019")
nodes.summary: The text details the Restricted Stock Units Plan 2019, including share-based payment arrangements with option series, grant dates, vesting periods, expiry dates, exercise prices, and fair values. It reports the weighted average fair value of stock units granted and inputs for the Black-Scholes pricing model (share price, volatility, option life, dividend yield, risk-free rate). It covers movements in share options during the year (beginning balance, granted, forfeited, exercised, ending balance, exercisable), the effect on profit or loss, stock units exercised, and options outstanding at year-end with remaining contractual life.

nodes.title: 49. EXPENDITURE ON CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY (CSR)
nodes.summary: The text covers Note 49 on Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) for Eicher Motors Limited, detailing expenditure for FY 2024-25 and FY 2023-24, including gross amounts required, amounts spent on asset construction/acquisition and other purposes, unspent amounts for ongoing and other projects, and disclosures on ongoing projects with opening/closing balances and transfers to separate CSR unspent accounts. It also describes CSR activities undertaken directly or through the Eicher Group Foundation, including Royal Enfield Social Mission projects and community initiatives near manufacturing plants. Additionally, Note 50 provides additional information as required by Schedule III, presenting share of net assets, profit or loss, other comprehensive income, and total comprehensive income for the parent, foreign subsidiaries, and Indian joint ventures for FY 2024-25 and FY 2023-24.

nodes.title: 51. IND AS 116 LEASES
nodes.summary: This note on IND AS 116 Leases covers the Group's lease contracts for buildings with terms of 2 to 20 years, including extension and termination options, and leases with short-term and low-value exemptions. It details the movement in right-of-use assets (land and buildings) with opening balance, depreciation, additions, adjustments, and closing balance. It classifies lease liabilities into current and non-current, and presents the movement in lease liabilities including opening balance, interest expense, lease payments, additions, adjustments, and closing balance. Contractual maturities of lease liabilities are analyzed by time bands. It also discloses lease expenses for short-term leases, the weighted average incremental borrowing rate (8% to 9.5%), liquidity risk assessment, and amounts recognized in profit or loss including depreciation, interest expense, and short-term lease expense.

nodes.title: 52. CAPITAL COMMITMENT
nodes.summary: The text covers capital commitments, noting contracts remaining to be executed on capital account not provided for at ₹295.75 crores (previous year ₹424.47 crores), and other commitments for purchase/sales orders, employee benefits, and union agreements, with no long-term or material non-cancellable contracts. It also details a proposed final dividend of ₹1,919.15 crores (₹70 per share) for FY2024-25, recommended by the Board on May 14, 2025, subject to shareholder approval, compared to the prior year's dividend of ₹1,397.45 crores (₹51 per share).

nodes.title: 54. RATIO ANALYSIS AND ITS ELEMENTS
nodes.summary: The text presents a ratio analysis table comparing March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024, including percentage changes and reasons for variance for current ratio, debt-equity, debt service coverage, return on equity, inventory turnover, trade receivable turnover, trade payable turnover, net capital turnover, net profit ratio, return on capital employed, and return on investment. It then details note 55 on audit trail requirements: the Holding Company's accounting software (SAP, payroll, and others) had audit trail enabled throughout the year except for certain modules (investments, inventories, traded goods, service-type warranties) where it was enabled during the year, and direct database changes where it was not enabled except in SAP after year-end and payroll software; no tampering occurred. Joint ventures VE Commercial Vehicles Limited and Eicher Polaris Private Limited also used accounting software with audit trail, enabled during the year for direct database changes in certain systems, with no tampering; prior-year audit trail was preserved for record retention.

nodes.title: 56. OTHER STATUTORY INFORMATION
nodes.summary: The text presents 'Other Statutory Information' for a group, covering non-default on loans and no wilful defaulter status; absence of Benami property proceedings; no revaluation of PP&E, intangibles, or right-of-use assets; balances with struck-off companies; no unregistered charges with ROC; no crypto/virtual currency trading; no fund transfers to intermediaries for ultimate beneficiaries; no receipt of funds with such understanding; no unrecorded surrendered income in tax assessments; no loans to promoters, directors, KMPs, or related parties; and compliance with prescribed company layers. It also includes signatures of auditors and board members with dates and locations.

nodes.summary: The text presents VE Commercial Vehicles Limited's consolidated balance sheet as of March 31, 2025, with comparative figures for March 31, 2024. It details assets categorized into non-current (property, plant, equipment, capital work-in-progress, intangible assets, right-of-use assets, investments, loans, other financial and non-current assets) and current assets (inventories, trade receivables, cash, bank balances, loans, other financial and current assets), with totals. Equity and liabilities are split into equity (share capital, other equity), non-controlling interests, non-current liabilities (borrowings, lease liabilities, other financial liabilities, provisions, deferred tax, other non-current liabilities), and current liabilities (borrowings, lease liabilities, trade payables, other financial liabilities, other current liabilities, provisions, current tax liabilities), with totals. The document includes auditor and board signatures, place, and date.

nodes.title: CONSOLIDATED STATEMENT OF PROFIT AND LOSS
nodes.summary: The section presents the consolidated statement of profit and loss for FY2025, detailing income, expenses, profit before tax, tax expense, profit for the year, other comprehensive income, total comprehensive income, and attribution to equity holders and non-controlling interests. It includes basic and diluted earnings per share, auditor and board signatures, and references the consolidated statement of cash flow. The cash flow statement covers operating activities (adjustments to reconcile profit before tax to net cash flows, working capital changes, taxes paid), investing activities (capital expenditures, asset sales, investments, interest received), and financing activities (borrowings, interest paid, lease liabilities, dividends), ending with net decrease in cash and cash equivalents and components of cash balances.

LLP, company secretary and CFO signatures, board approval signatures (Sonika Loganey, Vinod Aggarwal, Siddhartha Lal, Sofia Frandberg), and place/date. nodes.title: A. CASH FLOW FROM OPERATING ACTIVITIES
nodes.summary: The text presents a cash flow statement section for operating activities, starting with profit before tax. It details adjustments to reconcile profit before tax to net cash flows, including depreciation, gains on asset sales, exchange differences, interest income, impairment, and finance costs. It then shows operating profit before working capital changes, followed by working capital adjustments for non-current and current assets (loans, financial assets, other assets, inventories, trade receivables) and liabilities (financial liabilities, provisions, other liabilities, trade payables). It concludes with cash generated from operations, income taxes paid, and net cash flows from operating activities.

nodes.title: B. CASH FLOW FROM INVESTING ACTIVITIES
nodes.summary: The text presents the consolidated statement of cash flow from investing activities for VE Commercial Vehicles Limited for the years ended March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024. It details cash flows from purchases of property, plant, equipment, intangible assets, and capital work-in-progress; net proceeds from sale of assets; investments and redemptions in fixed deposits and government securities; acquisition of a subsidiary net of cash; and interest received. It provides net cash used in investing activities for both years, along with comparative figures and a reference to the integrated annual report.

nodes.title: C. CASH FLOW FROM FINANCING ACTIVITIES
nodes.summary: The text presents the cash flow from financing activities section, detailing negative figures for net cash flow used in financing, including proceeds from/(repayment) of short and long-term borrowings, interest paid, payment of lease liabilities, acquisition of non-controlling interests, and dividends paid. It shows net decrease in cash and cash equivalents, beginning and ending cash balances, and components of cash and cash equivalents (cash on hand, cheques/drafts, bank balances in current and deposit accounts). nodes.title: NOTICE OF 43RD (FORTY-THIRD) ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING
nodes.summary: The notice convenes Eicher Motors Limited's 43rd AGM on August 21, 2025, via video conferencing. Ordinary business includes adopting FY2025 financial statements, declaring a ₹70 dividend, and re-appointing Mr. Vinod Kumar Aggarwal as Director. Special business covers appointing secretarial and cost auditors, and approving related party transactions with VECV and Volvo Group India up to ₹4000 Crores. Additional sections provide procedures for joining the AGM via video conferencing and instructions for remote e-voting, including eligibility, voting periods, and NSDL e-voting methods. It also includes NSDL e-voting login methods, mobile app procedures, step-by-step voting instructions, guidelines for e-voting on the AGM day, and general guidelines for shareholders, including contact details and result declaration.

key_items: ELECTRONIC DISPATCH OF ANNUAL REPORT AND PROCESS FOR REGISTRATION OF EMAIL ID FOR OBTAINING COPY OF ANNUAL REPORT:
PROCEDURE TO RAISE QUESTIONS / SEEK CLARIFICATIONS:
nodes.summary: The text outlines an additional ODR mechanism for investor grievance resolution via a portal, and the availability of registers and certificates for inspection. It details the electronic dispatch of the Annual Report and the process for registering email IDs to obtain a copy, including provisions for unregistered members. It also specifies procedures for raising questions or seeking clarifications ahead of the AGM, registering as a speaker, and the company's right to limit questions and speakers for smooth conduct.

nodes.title: PROCEDURE FOR JOINING THE AGM THROUGH VIDEO CONFERENCING:
nodes.summary: The text outlines procedures for joining Eicher Motors Limited's AGM via video conferencing using the NSDL e-Voting system. It details access steps, retrieving lost credentials, and recommends laptops/desktops with stable internet, warning against mobile hotspots. Members can join from 12:30 p.m. IST. Institutional investors are encouraged to participate and can seek help via email. Assistance contacts for NSDL are provided, and VC attendees count toward quorum under Section 103 of the Companies Act, 2013.

nodes.title: INSTRUCTIONS FOR MEMBERS FOR REMOTE E-VOTING ARE AS UNDER:
nodes.summary: The text outlines instructions for members on remote e-voting for the 43rd AGM, in compliance with Section 108 of the Companies Act, 2013, Rule 20 of Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014, and SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. It specifies the e-voting facility provided by NSDL, the cut-off date of August 14, 2025, and the voting period from August 18 to August 20, 2025. It details eligibility for members holding shares in physical or dematerialized form, restrictions on vote changes, and that non-members should treat the notice as information only. It then explains the two-step NSDL e-voting process, including login methods for individual demat shareholders: OTP-based login, NSDL IDeAS facility (for registered and unregistered users), NSDL e-voting website, and the NSDL Speede mobile app.

nodes.summary: The notice instructs shareholders to update their mobile number and email ID in their demat accounts to access e-Voting. It details three login methods: OTP-based login for individual demat shareholders with NSDL (steps include entering DP ID, Client ID, PAN, verification code, and OTP); NSDL IDeAS facility with separate steps for registered and unregistered users; and the e-Voting website of NSDL (login via demat account number, password/OTP, and verification code). Each method guides users to the e-Voting page to cast votes remotely or join virtual meetings and vote.

nodes.title: D. e-Voting mobile application of NSDL
nodes.summary: The text details e-voting procedures for Eicher Motors shareholders. It covers the NSDL Speede mobile app with QR code for seamless voting. For individual demat shareholders with CDSL, it explains login via CDSL Easi/Easiest or direct demat/PAN access, and registration. For individual demat shareholders using depository participants, it describes login through demat credentials to access NSDL/CDSL e-voting. It includes helpdesk contacts for NSDL and CDSL technical issues. For non-individual demat and physical shareholders, it outlines NSDL e-voting website login steps, User ID formats by holding type, password retrieval/initial password details, forgot password options, OTP login, and terms acceptance.

nodes.title: Details on Step 2 are mentioned below:
nodes.summary: Step 2 of the NSDL e-Voting process explains how to cast votes electronically and join a General Meeting. After logging in, users see companies with active voting cycles and General Meetings. They select the relevant EVEN (e.g., 134609) to vote remotely or during the meeting, and click the VC/OAVM link to join virtually. The voting page opens, allowing selection of assent or dissent, verification or modification of share numbers, and submission with confirmation. A success message appears, and users can print the vote confirmation. Once confirmed, votes cannot be modified.

nodes.title: THE INSTRUCTIONS FOR MEMBERS FOR E-VOTING ON THE DAY OF THE AGM ARE AS UNDER:
nodes.summary: The text outlines instructions for members regarding e-voting on the day of the AGM. It states that the procedure is the same as for remote e-voting. It specifies eligibility based on being a member on the cut-off date and allows remote e-voters to attend but not vote again. It also identifies the contact person for e-voting grievances as the same person mentioned for remote e-voting and AGM through VC under Para 27.

nodes.title: 35. GENERAL GUIDELINES FOR SHAREHOLDERS FOR VOTING:
nodes.summary: This text outlines general guidelines for shareholders voting at Eicher Motors' 43rd AGM. It instructs corporate and institutional shareholders to submit board resolutions and authority letters via email or upload. It emphasizes password confidentiality and account lockout after five failed attempts, with reset options. It provides contact details for voting queries and states voting rights are proportional to shares held as of the cut-off date August 14, 2025, with joint holders' priority. It explains how new members can obtain login credentials. It names Vijay Gupta or Akshay Kakkar as Scrutinizers. It describes the AGM voting process, scrutinizer report, and declaration of results within two working days, with results published on specified websites. Company contact details and signatory are included.

nodes.title: EXPLANATORY STATEMENT PURSUANT TO SECTION 102 OF THE COMPANIES ACT, 2013
nodes.summary: This section’s explanatory statement under Section 102 covers four items. Item 4 seeks approval for appointing M/s. AGSB & Associates as Secretarial Auditors for five years, detailing regulatory compliance, firm background, fees, and board recommendation. Item 5 requests shareholder approval for material related party transactions between VECV and Volvo Group India up to ₹4,000 Crores for FY 2025-26, including justification, prior approvals, and voting restrictions. Item 6 proposes ratification of Cost Auditor remuneration for M/s. Jyothi Satish & Co. at ₹5,00,000 plus taxes for FY 2024-25. Finally, a notice regarding TDS on dividends outlines tax provisions for resident shareholders, including thresholds, PAN requirements, lower/nil tax deduction certificates, and Form 15G/15H submissions.

nodes.title: Item no. 4
nodes.summary: The explanatory statement under Section 102 of the Companies Act, 2013 concerns Item no. 4: the appointment of M/s. AGSB & Associates as Secretarial Auditors. It cites Sections 204 and Rule 9, and amended SEBI Regulation 24A effective April 1, 2025, requiring member approval, peer review, and limits of one five-year term for individuals or two for firms, excluding prior association before March 31, 2025. The Audit Committee and Board approved a five-year term (FY 2025-26 to FY 2029-30) subject to shareholder approval. It details the firm's prior service, role as auditors of VE Commercial Vehicles Ltd, signing partner Amit Gupta's qualifications, peer review certification, and expertise. It notes management satisfaction, consent and eligibility confirmations, fees of Rs. 4,50,000 for FY 2025-26 with a Rs. 6,00,000 ceiling thereafter plus expenses and separate certification fees, the Board's recommendation for an Ordinary Resolution, and no director or KMP interest.

nodes.title: Item no. 5
nodes.summary: The section addresses shareholder approval for material related party transactions (RPTs) under SEBI Regulation 23, specifically between Eicher Motors' unlisted material subsidiary VECV and Volvo Group India (VGIPL) for FY 2025-26, valued up to ₹4,000 Crores. It defines RPTs, explains the threshold exceedance (21.47% of consolidated turnover), and provides justification based on VECV's exclusive distribution of Volvo Trucks, growth plans, and dependence on VGIPL. Details include prior year approvals and actual transactions, arm's length pricing, Audit Committee and Board approvals, related party relationships, common directors, voting restrictions, and confirmation that transactions are in the ordinary course of business and shareholders' interest.

nodes.title: Item no. 5 (intro)
nodes.summary: The text informs shareholders about Regulation 23 of SEBI Listing Regulations, defining material related party transactions (RPTs) as those exceeding ₹1,000 Crores or 10% of annual consolidated turnover, requiring shareholder approval via ordinary resolution. It details the definition of RPTs under Regulation 2(1)(zc). It explains that Eicher Motors Limited seeks shareholder approval for RPTs between its unlisted material subsidiary, VE Commercial Vehicles Limited (VECV), and Volvo Group India Private Limited (VGIPL), a related party of VECV, even though the Company is not a party. The transactions for FY 2025-26 are expected to be up to ₹4,000 Crores, exceeding the threshold. Last year's approval and actual transaction value are noted. The transactions are in the ordinary course of business, at arm's length, and approved by the Audit Committee and Board. It includes details of the related party, relationship, and nature of transactions.

nodes.title: Details
nodes.summary: The text outlines details for a proposed related party transaction (RPT) between VECV and VGIPL for FY 2025-26, valued up to ₹4,000 Crores excluding taxes. It provides the percentage of the listed entity's consolidated turnover (21.47%) and VECV's standalone turnover (17.02%) represented by the transaction. Justification cites VECV's exclusive distribution of Volvo Trucks in India, growth plans in road construction, mining, logistics, and alternative fuel trucks. It notes prior approval for FY 2024-25 with actual transactions of ₹3,295 Crores. Background details VECV's business, Volvo Group's portfolio, VTI's contribution (14.06% of sales, ₹3,235 Crores revenue), and VECV's dependence on VGIPL. It also covers loan-related particulars (sl. no. 7), arm's length pricing (sl. no. 8), and related director/KMP details (sl. no. 9).

nodes.title: Details
nodes.summary: VTI's market leadership in premium trucks with 400+ Hp engines and nationwide service network is highlighted. Volvo Group's expansion plans include higher capacity mining trucks, road trains via VECV, and alternate energy solutions like LNG and electric trucks. The text details a proposed related party transaction between VECV and VGIPL to procure Volvo trucks and related parts/services for up to ₹4,000 Crores in FY 2025-26, based on arm's length pricing. It outlines the approval process involving the Audit Committee, Board, and shareholders, and confirms the transactions are in the ordinary course of business and in shareholders' interest. Common directors and voting restrictions are noted.

nodes.title: Item No. 6:
nodes.summary: The text outlines Item No. 6 of a board meeting notice for Eicher Motors Limited, regarding ratification of Cost Auditor remuneration under Section 148 of the Companies Act, 2013. The Board, on August 8, 2024, approved the appointment of M/s. Jyothi Satish & Co., Cost Accountants, for auditing cost records for FY 2024-25. Based on Audit Committee recommendations, the Board proposes remuneration of ₹5,00,000 plus taxes and reimbursements, seeking shareholder approval via Ordinary Resolution. It confirms no Directors or Key Managerial Personnel are interested in the resolution. The notice is issued by order of the Board.

nodes.title: Atul Sharma
nodes.summary: The text is a notice regarding Tax Deduction at Source (TDS) on dividends by a company, referencing Note 9 of the 43rd AGM Notice. It outlines TDS provisions under the Income-tax Act, 1961, and Finance Act, 2020, effective April 1, 2020, stating dividends are taxable in members' hands. For resident shareholders, it specifies: no TDS if total dividend ≤ ₹10,000 and PAN is available; TDS at 10% if valid PAN is updated and no exemption sought, or 20% if PAN is invalid/inoperative; lower/nil tax deduction certificate under section 197 can be submitted with PAN copy. It includes notes on PAN-Aadhaar linking and documents required. For resident members submitting Form 15G/15H, no TDS applies if eligibility conditions are met, requiring PAN copy and the form. The text includes a table summarizing rates and documents.

nodes.title: COMMUNICATION ON TAX DEDUCTION AT SOURCE (TDS) ON DIVIDEND
nodes.summary: This section details TDS on dividends under the Income-tax Act, 1961, effective April 1, 2020. For resident shareholders, it covers the ₹10,000 threshold, 10% TDS with valid PAN, 20% for invalid/inoperative PAN, Section 197 certificates, and required documents like Form 15G/15H and self-declarations for exempt entities. For non-residents, it addresses Tax Treaty benefits under Section 90, 20% plus surcharge/cess or lower treaty rate, required documents (PAN, Tax Residency Certificate, Form 10F, SEBI registration, Format SD2), withholding for various shareholder categories (FPIs, sovereign wealth funds, pension funds), Section 206AA, submission deadlines, RTA process, compliance checks, multiple accounts, Rule 37BA(2), reassessment rights, refunds, and indemnity. It also includes Eicher Motors' guidelines, SD1-SD7 forms, August 8, 2025 deadline, and a GRI Content Index from the 2024-25 Integrated Annual Report.

nodes.title: A. RESIDENT SHAREHOLDERS:
nodes.summary: This document outlines TDS provisions on dividends under the Income-tax Act, 1961, effective April 1, 2020, where dividends are taxable in members' hands and the company must deduct TDS. For resident shareholders, no TDS applies if total dividend is up to ₹10,000 with valid PAN. Otherwise, TDS is 10% with valid PAN, 20% for no/invalid/inoperative PAN, or the rate in a Section 197 lower/nil withholding certificate. It details required documents: PAN, Form 15G/15H for eligible individuals, Section 197 certificates, and self-declarations with evidence for exempt entities like LIC, GIC, AIFs, mutual funds, and others under Sections 194, 196, or 197A, including CBDT Circular 18/2017 cases.

nodes.title: B. NON-RESIDENT SHAREHOLDERS:
nodes.summary: The section covers provisions for non-resident shareholders under Section 90 of the IT Act, allowing them to opt for beneficial Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (Tax Treaty) rates. It specifies the applicable tax rate as 20% plus surcharge and cess, or the Tax Treaty rate, whichever is lower. Required documents to claim Tax Treaty benefits include a self-attested PAN copy, Tax Residency Certificate for FY 2025-26, electronically generated Form 10F, SEBI registration certificate for FIIs/FPIs, and a self-declaration (Format SD2) certifying continued tax residency, eligibility for beneficial treaty rate, no reason to believe claim is impaired, and beneficial ownership of shareholding and dividend. It outlines tax withholding requirements for dividend payments to various shareholder categories, including non-residents, AIFs, FPIs, sovereign wealth funds, and pension funds, specifying applicable tax rates, required documents, conditions for beneficial tax treaty rates, Section 206AA provisions for missing/invalid PAN, submission deadlines, RTA submission process, compliance check functionality, multiple accounts with different statuses, Rule 37BA(2) declarations, company's right to reassess declarations, refund options, and indemnity for misrepresentation. It provides Eicher Motors' guidelines for shareholders on tax declarations for dividend income, explaining that members with multiple accounts under different residential statuses will be taxed at the higher applicable rate, submission instructions for forms like Form 15G/15H and self-declarations SD1-SD7, along with PAN, via the RTA's website or email by August 8, 2025, the company's right to independently assess and deduct higher taxes if declarations are found contrary, and notes that members can claim refunds but cannot hold the company liable. It also covers Rule 37BA(2) declarations for tax credit to another person, indemnity for misrepresentation, directs queries to the RTA, and includes download links for all forms. Additionally, it presents a GRI Content Index from an Integrated Annual Report 2024-25, mapping various GRI Standards to specific disclosures and corresponding sections with page numbers.

It lists required documents to claim Tax Treaty benefits: self-attested PAN copy, Tax Residency Certificate for FY 2025-26, electronically generated Form 10F, SEBI registration certificate for FIIs/FPIs, and a self-declaration (Format SD2) certifying continued tax residency, eligibility for beneficial treaty rate, no reason to believe claim is impaired, and beneficial ownership of shareholding and dividend.

It covers compliance check functionality for PAN, multiple accounts with different statuses, Rule 37BA(2) declarations for other persons, company's right to reassess declarations, refund options, indemnity for misrepresentation, and provides links to forms and self-declaration formats (SD1–SD7).

nodes.title: Eicher Motors Tax Declaration Guidelines for Shareholders
key_items: For all members (Resident and Non- Resident)
nodes.summary: The page outlines Eicher Motors' guidelines for shareholders (resident and non-resident) on tax declarations for dividend income. It explains that members with multiple accounts under different residential statuses will be taxed at the higher applicable rate. It provides submission instructions for forms like Form 15G/15H and self-declarations SD1-SD7, along with PAN, via the RTA's website or email by August 8, 2025. It details the company's right to independently assess and deduct higher taxes if declarations are found contrary, and notes that members can claim refunds but cannot hold the company liable. It also covers Rule 37BA(2) declarations for tax credit to another person, indemnity for misrepresentation, and directs queries to the RTA. Download links for all forms are included.
